海底地形、内波与叶绿素分布的多尺度耦合研究进展
赵    辉1，  伍世文1，  吴梅林2
（1.广东海洋大学 化学与环境学院, 广东 湛江 524088；2.中国科学院南海海洋研究所 热带海洋环境与岛
礁生态全国重点实验室, 广东 广州 510301）
摘    要：本文系统分析了不同海底地形对内波的影响及调控叶绿素的机制。在内波生成、传播和耗散的
不同区域中，内波通过垂直混合、水平输运与改变光环境等方式，直接或间接地影响叶绿素的分布，这
种作用强烈依赖海底地形。不同地形通过影响内波生消演变的过程，促使数种作用机制以不同的方式
组合，共同塑造独特的叶绿素分布格局。内波作为高频物理过程，通过与海底地形的相互作用，对海洋
初级生产力和生态系统产生不可忽视的生态效应，未来需融合多源数据并结合人工智能等新兴技术深
化研究。
关键词：内波； 海底地形； 叶绿素分布； 海洋初级生产力

Research progress on multi-scale coupling of seafloor topography,
internal waves and Chlorophyll distribution
Zhao Hui1,    Wu Shiwen1,    Wu Meilin2
(1.Faculty  of  Chemistry  and  Environment  Science,  Guangdong  Ocean  University,  Zhanjiang  524088,  China;  2.State  Key
Laboratory  of  Tropical  Oceanography,  South  China  Sea  Institute  of  Oceanology,  Chinese  Academy  of  Sciences,  Guangzhou
510301, China)
Abstract: This paper systematically analyzes the influence of different seabed topographies on internal waves
and  the  mechanisms  by  which  they  regulate  chlorophyll  distribution.  In  regions  where  internal  waves  are
generated,  propagated,  and  dissipated,  they  influence  the  distribution  of  marine  chlorophyll  through  vertical
mixing,  horizontal  transport,  and  modifications  of  the  light  environment.  These  effects  strongly  depend  on
seabed topography, as different topographic features influence the generation and evolution of internal waves,
leading  to  various  mechanisms  acting  in  different  combinations  and  shaping  distinct  chlorophyll  distribution
patterns.  As  high-frequency  physical  processes,  internal  waves  interact  with  seabed  topography  and  exert
significant  ecological  effects  on  oceanic  primary  productivity  and  marine  ecosystems.  Future  studies  should
integrate multi-source observations and emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence, to further advance
research in this field.
Key words: internal waves; seafloor topography; Chlorophyll distribution; marine primary productivity

作为发生在密度跃层上的一类高频波动，其生态
效应因观测手段限制而长期被忽视，相关过程多

被参数化处理[6]。随着高分辨率观测技术的普
及，近年来的研究表明，内波活动对海洋上层生
态系统的调控可能具有与其他大尺度过程同样
的重要性。与持续数周至数月的涡旋或季风等
过程不同，内波可在更小的空间与时间尺度上产
生脉冲式的施肥效应[7]。与偶发的、高强度的台
风不同，虽然单次内波作用强度相对较弱，但其
发生频率极高，部分海区甚至每日均可观测到内
波发生[8-11]。数值模拟研究结果显示，单次短周
期内波扰动即可诱发深层叶绿素最大值持续振
荡，且影响长达数周[12]，凸显了高频物理过程对
生态系统动态的长期调控能力。另有72 h高分
辨率连续生态监测结果首次揭示，浮游植物群落
对内波强化上升流的响应存在12 h至16 h的滞
后[13]，如果使用传统低频次观测方式则完全无法
捕捉这种快速、异步的复杂生态过程。因此，这
种由内波引发的集少成多式的生态效应便具备
了不可忽视的研究价值。
同时，内波的生消演变也与海底地形密切相
关，内波的扩散路径与稳定状态等始终受地形作
用影响，其能量衰减主要发生于斜坡地貌处的破
碎过程中，这种现象对海洋湍流混合以及经向翻
转环流具有重要意义[14]。特定的地形可进一步
强化该类作用，例如，安达曼海南部双海槛地貌
引发的共振效应使内孤立波振幅提升一倍，显著
增强了海洋上层水体混合效果与营养盐供给效
率[15]。
另外，海洋物理过程对浮游植物生态系统的
影响通常表现出明显的跨尺度耦合特征，海盆尺
度和区域尺度的海底地形结构在很大程度上控
制了内波的生成位置及传播路径，而内波在传播
过程中能够影响海洋上层环境和浮游植物的空
间分布特征，这种由地形控制、经由内波动力过
程传递并最终作用于生态系统的关系，构成了海
洋物理−生物相互作用的重要表现形式。
因此，在台风等相对更宏观过程的生态效应
研究已较为系统的背景下，深入分析内波尤其是
在不同海底地貌条件下的内波的特殊作用，对于
更全面掌握海洋物理−生物耦合机制具有重要价
值。本综述致力于系统梳理该领域研究动态，从
作用机制层面阐明不同类型海底地貌如何通过
影响内波生消演变驱动营养盐迁移、水平输运及
光环境调节等关键物理过程，最终塑造海洋叶绿
素空间分布格局。为了更直观地展示海底地形、
内波动力过程与叶绿素响应之间的关系，构建了
海底地形−内波−叶绿素分布多尺度耦合概念框
架（图1）。该框架展示了海底地形通过控制内
波动力过程，经由4种核心机制影响叶绿素分布
的多尺度耦合关系：（1） 垂向混合与营养盐输送：内
波破碎诱发湍流混合，将深层营养盐跨密度面向
上输送至真光层，补充浮游植物生长所需；（2）水
平输运与生物量再分配：内波引起的非线性平流
效应及斯托克斯漂移，驱动浮游植物在空间上重
新分布，形成叶绿素斑块与条带状分布；（3）光环
境调制：内波引发的等密度面周期性起伏改变浮
游植物的光照暴露，影响光合作用效率与初级生
产力；（4）多机制协同响应：在环礁、海脊等复杂
地形区，上述多种机制常同步发生并相互耦合，
共同放大生态效应。该框架概括了本文主线：大
尺度海底地形控制内波生成与传播，中尺度内波
动力过程通过上述四类机制传递能量与物质，最
终在更小尺度上塑造叶绿素的时空分布格局。

 1   内波作用下叶绿素的区域响应
 1.1    内波生成区域
在海峡、海脊等强潮流与复杂地形耦合作用
区域，内波的生成活动尤为活跃[16]，且内波生成
的强度与地形粗糙程度呈正相关关系，坡度越
陡、地形越复杂，内潮振幅越大，其最直接的生
态效应表现为等密度面振荡引起的叶绿素垂向
结构变化。
吕宋海峡是目前公认的全球内潮强度最高
的发源地之一，其产生的内潮向西传播进入南中
国海，继而孕育出全球规模最大的内波系统[17-18]。
垂向观测结果表明，内波活动可将富含叶绿素的
水 体 输 送 至 次 表 层 叶 绿 素 浓 度 最 大 值 层 以 下
100 m以上深度；与此同时，研究发现该区域存
在 空 间 尺 度 约 50  km、 表 层 叶 绿 素 a浓 度 达
0.2～0.5 mg/m3的高值区域，与内波活跃区的位置
一致[19-20]。类似地，印度尼西亚海域望加锡海峡
也是全球内潮生成热点之一，该区域的内潮在东
南季风期间（7月—9月）叶绿素a浓度显著提升，
且叶绿素a浓度存在与大潮−小潮周期（约14.8 d）
同步的波动，波动达0.06 ～ 0.1 mg Chl/m3[21]。
同样，在由风强迫或潮汐生成的内波作用
下，密度跃层周期性振荡导致叶绿素a浓度最大
值层也随之同步移动，在低潮期间，内波能将富
含叶绿素的深层水体向上抬升，使叶绿素浓度最
大值层上移，高潮期间则反之[22]，证明了内波在
生成区的扰动已开始塑造叶绿素垂直分布的格
局。由此可见，在生成区，大尺度地形与潮流的
相互作用激发内波，内波通过等密度面起伏开始
影响叶绿素的垂向结构，构成地形、内波及生态
响应耦合链条的起点。
 1.2    内波传播区域
在传播阶段，海底地形通过影响内波传播路
径及能量衰减过程，持续影响营养盐输送，塑造
独特的叶绿素分布特征。早期观测研究指出，内
波在深海过境时可将深层营养盐快速带进真光
层，直接提高真光层叶绿素浓度，进而促进表层
浮游植物生长[23]。吕宋海峡产生的内波在向南
海西北部传播过程中，直接导致东沙群岛附近海
域叶绿素a浓度出现局部增强的现象[24]。另外，
长期卫星数据显示，春、夏两季东沙环礁的叶绿
素a浓度呈现持续北高南低的不对称分布格局，
这正是内波传播至北侧浅水区后的结果[25]。即
使在北极海域，内波传播过程也使密度跃层处的
营 养 盐 向 上 通 量 增 加 了 一 个 量 级 ， 进 而 推 动
20 m深度附近次表层叶绿素a浓度最大值的增
加[26]。
此外，在全球变暖的背景下，气候模型预测
上层海洋层化的持续增强可能会加快全球大部
分海域内潮的传播速度[27]，预示着未来内波可能
会显著改变全球大洋的叶绿素分布特征和生态
系统结构。相较于生成区的局地垂向扰动，内波
在传播阶段体现为能量与物质的远距离输运，进
而影响叶绿素的空间再分配，是多尺度耦合关键
的中间环节。
 1.3    内波耗散区域
内波耗散是能量集中释放的环节，该过程主
要发生在大陆坡浅水区，往往能够塑造叶绿素的
空间分布。当非线性内波从深海盆传播至大陆
坡发生耗散时，其波形从“凹陷波”转变为“抬
升波”，经此过程后的内波在东沙环礁大陆坡支
撑起118 ～232 mg C/（m2· d）的新生产力[28]。当
大振幅内波在泰国斯米兰群岛斜坡处耗散时，在
受内波影响强烈的西侧区域，优势珊瑚Porites
lutea组织中的虫黄藻叶绿素a含量显著高于东
侧[29]。此外，当内波传播至浅水区后可形成具有
冷核、被陡峭梯度层包围的孤立水团（Boluses），
这些Boluses能独立向岸传播，在近岸形成清晰
的叶绿素a浓度条带与斑块化分布特征[10]。
综上所述，内波在生成、传播和耗散各阶段
均显著塑造叶绿素分布，各阶段主导物理过程不
同：生成区以等密度面起伏为主，耗散区以湍流
混合为主，而水平输运与光环境调制则贯穿多阶
段。这一从生成区、传播区再到耗散区的链条
正是地形、内波及生态响应多尺度耦合的具体
路径。
 2   内波影响叶绿素分布的几类机制
 2.1    垂向混合驱动的营养盐输送
内波对营养盐垂向输运的影响主要通过两
类不同的物理机制实现。内波传播会引起等密
第 x 期 赵    辉，等:    海底地形、内波与叶绿素分布的多尺度耦合研究进展 3
度面的周期性起伏，使得深层水体及其所含的叶
绿素和营养盐随密度面发生垂向位移，这种等密
度面抬升（isopycnal heaving）通常只会导致叶绿
素浓度最大值水层位置的暂时变化，而不会产生
显著的跨密度面物质交换。相比之下，当内波传
播至陆坡或浅水区发生破碎时，其产生的强剪切
流可诱发Kelvin-Helmholtz不稳定，从而形成湍
流混合并实现跨密度面的营养盐输送[30]。这一
过程才是将深层营养盐真正补给至真光层的重
要机制。
内波在向大陆坡、海脊等地形传播时，其振
幅往往逐渐增大并表现出明显的非线性特征，当
内波振幅增大到一定程度时，容易发生波破碎或
剪切不稳定，从而产生强烈的湍流混合[31]，这种
混合能将下层富含营养盐的冷水向上输送至真
光层，为浮游植物生长繁殖提供条件，是内波影
响海洋初级生产力最直接、最重要途径。
大陆坡与陆架边缘是内波从深海向浅海传
播时能量集中消耗的区域，也是观测捕捉该效应
的重点区域。例如，夏季凯尔特海大陆边缘表面
存在一个约100 km宽的带状冷却区，早期研究指
出这是由于内波破碎导致湍流混合，将较冷的下
层水带到表层的结果，而非简单的上升流效应[32]。
此后，随着更精密观测技术的应用，研究者发现，
夏季凯尔特海陆架边缘向次表层叶绿素浓度最
大值水层的硝酸盐垂直通量存在显著的大潮、
小潮差异，并证实内波可通过间歇性混合的方式
实现“脉冲式”的营养补给[33]。基于数值模型
的研究从时间动态层面捕捉并量化了这种“脉
冲式”的特征。美国马萨诸塞湾海盆西缘陆坡
的营养盐垂向通量通常维持在较低水平，当内波
波包过境时，营养盐垂向通量会在短时间内急剧
升高，瞬时峰值较背景值高出2～3个数量级，随
后又迅速回落[7]，这种营养补给模式对维系季节
性层结水体中的深层叶绿素浓度最大值层具有
重要作用。
内波对水体混合的作用在凸起的海底地形
区域同样显著，当内潮经过大西洋中脊海域时，
其引发的垂向混合可使输送至深层叶绿素浓度
最大值层的跨密度硝酸盐通量提高近一个数量
级，且该过程表现出显著的潮汐周期调控特征[34]。
海底峡谷是陆架与深海之间物质与能量交换的
通道，这种独特的地形能够聚集和放大内波的能
量。例如，纳扎雷峡谷的内波通过垂直输送作用
可将深层叶绿素浓度最大值层抬升到近表层，形
成规模显著的叶绿素富集斑块，局部区域初级生
产力增幅最高可达8.7%/d[35]。此外，内波在强上
升流环境中依然具备调控作用，内波活动在大潮
时期可大幅强化湍流混合程度，并提升硝酸盐通
量，在上升流间歇期维持了西班牙维戈湾近50%
的初级生产力[36]。
综上所述，在不同海底地形条件下，内波驱
动的湍流混合均是打破层结、实现营养盐垂向
输运的核心过程。
 2.2    水平输运主导的生物量再分配
内波不仅能驱动垂向混合，也能引起显著的
水平输运（平流），在空间上重新分布浮游生物[37]。
在海峡等受地形约束显著的区域中，内波水平平
流效应往往更强。例如，内波在直布罗陀海峡对
浮游生物分布存在抽吸和输送的作用机制，富含
叶绿素的沿岸水体在内波形成初期被抽吸至海
峡中心区域，随后随内波波列持续向前推移，形
成移动性的叶绿素富集区域[38]。另外，龙目海峡
的强内波活动可推动巴厘岛南部沿岸的高叶绿
素浓度区域显著向西延伸，证实内波的水平平流
效应可调控海峡区域浮游生物的分布[39]。
内波水平输运的生态效应并不局限于海峡，
相关研究显示，陆架边缘的内潮水平通量同样可
维持浮游植物的高生产力，且效果可能比垂向混
合更加显著。内潮在南加州湾陆架海域向岸一
侧传播时，其所携带的硝酸盐通量平均可支撑
774 mg C/（m2 ·d）的新生产力，研究指出，比起垂
向混合，内潮诱导的水平输运才是实现营养盐向
陆架输送的主要途径，同时解释了南加州湾内陆
架持续存在浮游生物高生物量的现象[40]。近年
来的数值模拟研究表明，内波场中的斯托克斯漂
移等非线性平流效应，会显著改变浮游生物在波
峰、波谷等不同波相位的滞留时间，进而导致浮
游植物的光照获取量出现明显差异[41]。对于振
幅较小的线性内波，由于水体运动近似呈对称振
荡，粒子轨迹接近闭合，因此产生的斯托克斯漂
移通常较弱；而在振幅较大的非线性内孤立波
4 海    洋    环    境    科    学 第 46 卷
中，波动的非线性显著增强，粒子轨迹不再完全
闭合，从而产生更为明显的斯托克斯漂移及净物
质输运[42-43]。这类针对“生物光暴露”的物理
调控过程会影响浮游植物的生长效率与群落竞
争。内波的这种水平输运过程既能直接完成生
物量的空间重组，形成观测记录中叶绿素a斑块
状、条带状等分布形态，也能通过调控生物的光
环境暴露过程间接参与生态系统的结构与功能
调控。
 2.3    光环境的调节
在层化明显且内波活跃的地形区域中，内波
传播会引发水体等密度面周期性的垂向移动，直
接且快速地改变浮游植物所处的相对位置，进而
通过光照条件的变化影响光合作用[44]。这同样
是内波影响初级生产与叶绿素空间分布的重要
途径之一，其效果在光照作为浮游植物生长主要
制约因素的真光层下半部与深层叶绿素浓度极
大值层中更加显著。该机制与营养盐输运机制
可能呈现协同效应，也可能存在其他复杂的相互
作用。
早期，Lande和Yentsch[45]的研究为这种光
调制效应提供了理论支撑，该研究从理论模型的
角度指出，除了常见的促进营养盐输送外，内波
还能通过垂直位移的方式来“平均化”光照，显
著提高下层透光带浮游植物的有效光照。因光
照强度随水深呈指数级衰减，当浮游植物在内波
作用下短暂上升至较浅水层时，其获取到的光照
增量远远高于下沉至较深水层时的光照损耗量，
这 使 得 初 级 生 产 力 在 富 营 养 盐 水 域 中 可 提 升
65%至数倍，同时让补偿深度拓展5～10 m，影
响 效 果 显 著 且 不 可 忽 视 。 随 后 “ 交 叉 深 度
（crossover depth）”概念的提出进一步拓展了该
理论，Holloway等[46]认为，在交叉深度以上的浅
水层中，内波导致的光照波动会因光合作用的
“负曲率”而抑制平均初级生产，这是由于浮游
植物光合作用速率与光照强度之间通常呈向下
凹的非线性关系，在相同平均光照条件下，光照
的周期性波动可能导致平均光合速率低于稳定
光 照 条 件 下 的 水 平 ， 这 一 现 象 通 常 与 Jensen’s
inequality所描述的非线性效应有关[47]，同时又因
生物体的平均光照环境被改变，在该深度以深时
内波活动反而增强了平均初级生产。之后，美国
阿拉斯加州Toolik湖的原位培养试验结果显示，
模拟内波运动特征的光照波动可使浮游植物的
光合作用效率提升200%[48]，为该理论提供了强
有力的实验佐证。
此外，浮游植物随内波起伏导致接收光照量
的差异，会引发浮游植物群落产生复杂的反应及
群落层面的变化。加利福尼亚湾的高频观测结
果显示，内波在传播过程中将已适应弱光环境的
深层浮游植物（如深水型硅藻）抬升至表层强光
区域，导致此类浮游植物的同化数（光合作用核
心参数）出现即时且显著的降低，该研究表明，如
果在动力活跃的海域忽视内波这类高频物理扰
动对浮游植物的瞬时作用，那么基于固定参数构
建的生产力估算模型将可能出现较大偏差[49]。
高时间分辨率生态监测的应用，为解析浮游
植物群落对内波响应的动态特征等提供了技术
支撑。Ma等[50]通过一次持续154 h的观测，提
出寡营养海区浮游植物群落对内波响应的“三
层稳态结构”模型，系统阐明了上层（营养盐限
制）、深层叶绿素浓度最大值层（光−营养盐共同
限制）和下层（光限制）群落分别受营养盐补给、
光照条件优化及摄食压力调节的差异化响应机
制。这些研究将内波生态学从单一叶绿素浓度
变化层面拓展至浮游植物生理生态特征与群落
结构演替的深度，明确了内波作为物理驱动因素
在通过调控光环境塑造微型生物生态系统动态
过程中的核心地位。
 2.4    多重物理机制在特定地形下的协同响应
内波多样的物理−生物耦合机制与特定地形
叠加的影响不仅体现在对初级生产力的增加上，
对生态系统更具有深远影响。环礁与海脊系统
正是这类效应的代表，在这类具有显著地形起伏
的海域中，内波活动往往更加活跃，不同物理过
程之间也更容易发生相互耦合。
环礁及珊瑚礁环境凭借独特的浅水地貌与
极高的生态价值，成为研究内波生态效应的天然
试验场，对内波的生态效应研究已从单纯的叶绿
素浓度变化层面，拓展至生态系统健康状态与稳
定程度的维系层面。现场观测与遥感技术结合
的研究证实，内波能使东沙环礁附近海域的叶绿
第 x 期 赵    辉，等:    海底地形、内波与叶绿素分布的多尺度耦合研究进展 5
素 a浓 度 和 净 初 级 生 产 力 分 别 提 高 43%和
37%[51]。之后多项观测研究进一步揭示了内波
对珊瑚礁生态系统的影响效应，东沙环礁附近海
域的内波将富含营养盐的底层冷水推向礁坪，输
送的硝酸盐通量约为无内波时的4倍，促使珊瑚
共生藻光合效率提高15%～20%，同时使礁坪水
温最大降低2.0 ℃，缓解了当今全球变暖背景下
珊瑚白化的风险[52]。这种施肥与降温的协同作
用为珊瑚礁提供了关键的营养支持，大幅强化了
珊瑚礁生态系统应对全球气候变化的能力。
除环礁与珊瑚礁系统外，另一典型类型为海
脊地形对水层−底栖耦合系统的强化作用。例
如，内波在美国缅因湾Cashes Ledge海脊可引发
最大27 m的垂向运移，并以脉冲式影响方式将
次表层叶绿素浓度高值层水体输送至浅水岩质
海底，使底栖生境的叶绿素a浓度在短时间内提
高2～3倍[53]。该过程形成了由物理过程驱动的
高效直接传输路径，实现了上层海洋初级生产合
成有机物质向底栖滤食类生物的快速转运。该
作用机制极可能广泛存在于全球诸多地貌特征
相近的海域，对深海碳循环过程和维持底栖生物
多样性等方面具有深远影响。
为进一步梳理不同物理机制对叶绿素分布
的影响及其生态响应，对相关研究进行了总结整
理，具体列于表1，从不同维度呈现了地形控制
内波、内波通过多机制影响生态响应的耦合框
架（图1）。内波对海洋叶绿素特征的影响呈现
多过程、多尺度的复杂关系，垂向混合作用输送
营养盐，水平平流运动实现生物量重新分配，光
环境调控则引发生物生理机能与群落结构的响
应变化，这些作用机制在不同地形条件下以不同
的方式耦合，共同塑造海洋表层与次表层生物的
分布格局。

 3   挑战与展望
 3.1    核心挑战
前人研究已揭示了海底地形可通过影响内
波生消演变过程，进一步调控叶绿素分布及海洋
生态响应。然而，由于内波具有强非线性、高时
空变化及多尺度耦合等特征，目前在观测、生态
效应解析等方面仍面临诸多挑战。
现有的观测手段仍难以同时解析内波快速
演变及其生态响应的跨尺度过程。在遥感观测
上 ， 光 学 卫 星 观 测 内 波 被 局 限 在 太 阳 耀 斑 区
（ solar  flare  region） 或 月 球 耀 斑 条 件 （ moon  flare
conditions）下[54]；合成孔径雷达（SAR）则较光学
卫星时间分辨率更低，扫描宽度更窄，难以连续追
踪同一内波事件，更无法捕捉内波短时的演变（如
破碎）等[55-56]。SAR图像仅反映海面的粗糙度，而
非内波自身的水下结构，通过这种海表信号反演
内波波幅等参数需要依赖复杂的物理模型[57-59]，
6 海    洋    环    境    科    学 第 46 卷
且易受船只尾迹、海洋锋面及海洋生态过程等
因素的干扰，此类过程会在SAR图像中产生与
内波高度相似的明暗条纹，存在误判风险[60-61]。
在原位观测中，由于内波传播速度快、波包空间
尺度大[62]，传统船载观测难以持续跟踪完整过
程，传统的锚定潜标（系泊）虽可获取连续时间序
列数据，但空间覆盖有限。近年来广泛应用的水
下滑翔机能够提高剖面观测能力，但其布设密
度、采样频率及传播路径预判误差等问题，仍限
制了对内波过程的高精度刻画[63]。
数 值 模 拟 是 研 究 内 波 生 态 效 应 的 重 要 手
段。内波既有几十米的边界层微结构，也存在数
百公里波列的大尺度演化，单一分辨率模型难以
同时解析不同尺度的过程[64]。传统海洋环流模
型的湍流闭合方案会显著抑制内波传播并导致
虚假耗散，且内孤立波与中尺度涡等其他过程的
相互作用会显著改变内波特性及其对叶绿素分
布的影响，又进一步提高了模拟的复杂性与计算
成本[65-67]。
在生态效应层面，内波引起叶绿素浓度的变
化，一方面只是受到单纯的物理过程影响，另一
方面是生物新生产作用，两种效应在观测中往往
叠加呈现，而这两种过程所代表的生态含义截然
不同，单纯依靠叶绿素数据无法回答内波究竟是
重新分配了现有生物量，还是真正刺激了新生产
力的增加与碳的固定。如何从叶绿素a浓度的
时空变化中分离这两种效应，是准确理解内波生
态作用的难题。
内波对浮游植物的影响存在滞后性[68]，如内
孤立波的时间尺度往往只有数小时，而浮游植物
的生理响应、群落结构变化以及初级生产力等
变化则可能需要更长时间才能显现，单一的瞬时
采样无法捕捉这种动态过程，且不同浮游植物类
群对内波扰动的响应存在显著差异[69]，这些特征
对观测策略提出了极高要求。
非常规模态内波的生态效应研究目前几乎
处于空白，以往观测研究的大多是第一模态内
波，对于其他模态内波的研究非常少[70]，但近年
观测发现，第二模态甚至更高模态的内波比常规
模态内波产生强流发生的深度更深，这类内波在
具有超临界地形和显著正压潮汐的河口系统等
特定地形条件下同样活跃，且能引发强烈的湍流
混合[71]，其对叶绿素格局的影响和对初级生产力
的贡献值得深入探究。
总体而言，当前研究的瓶颈在于如何实现内
波动力过程与生态响应的跨尺度协同观测与耦
合解析。
 3.2    展 望
当前，深度学习、人工智能等技术在海洋遥
感识别内波的领域大放异彩，利用新兴技术克服
传统观测方式效率低、依赖人工判读的问题，使
大范围、高频次内波观测成为可能。未来应大
力推进多技术融合，为高效利用海量卫星数据探
测内波提供关键的技术支撑。例如，将多源观测
数据融入数值模型中，有助于验证内波在百公里
尺度上的分布，同时校准在几十米尺度上的混合
过程，为理解内波对叶绿素分布的影响机制提供
可靠工具。
近年来生物地球化学Argo浮标（BGC-Argo）
的大规模布放，为深层叶绿素浓度最大值及其时
空变化特征的观测提供了新手段，浮标能弥补卫
星遥感“只能看表层”的局限，提供从表层到深
海的全球实时数据，显著拓展了海洋内部生物地
球化学过程的观测能力，尤其适用于关注次表层
叶绿素浓度最大值层动态的内波生态研究。新
一 代 增 强 型 BGC-Argo（ eBGC-Argo） 正 向 多 参
数、高精度和智能化方向发展，其可集成高光谱
光学、颗粒物成像、AI分类及深层碳通量观测
等功能，这些技术进步使研究协同多源数据成为
可能。例如，引入颗粒有机碳（POC）通量等生物
地球化学参数数据作为辅助证据，有助于判断内
波是否真正促进了浮游植物的新生产，而非仅导
致已有生物量的重新分配，进而可将内波生态学
研究从单一的叶绿素浓度变化层面，拓展到浮游
植物生理生态及群落演替等层面，对未来评估海
洋碳循环作用等方面具有重要科学价值。
未来研究需要从多尺度、多角度整合观测与

title: 中华人民共和国生态环境法典
summary: 我国首部以“法典”命名的法律，采用“适度法典化”模式，整合污染防治、生态保护、绿色低碳发展、生态环境责任等编，吸收并废止环境保护法、水污染防治法等10部单行法，兼容保留长江保护法等单行法。2026年3月12日通过、8月15日施行，现行有效。
note: 2026年3月12日第十四届全国人大第四次会议通过（主席令第七十号），2026年8月15日施行。明确吸收并同步废止环境保护法、海洋环境保护法、水污染防治法、环境影响评价法等10部法律；长江保护法、湿地保护法等作为保留单行法继续有效。；人民日报全文版（2026-03-16）；另见中国人大网/生态环境部。法典共5编1242条，水污染防治见第二编第三分编（第七至十章）。

title: 城镇排水与污水处理条例
summary: 为加强城镇排水与污水处理管理、保障设施安全运行、防治城镇水污染和内涝灾害而制定的行政法规，规定规划与建设、排水许可、污水处理、设施维护与保护、内涝防治及法律责任。2013年公布，2014年施行，是城镇水环境治理的重要依据。
note: 2013年9月18日国务院第24次常务会议通过，2013年10月2日公布，2014年1月1日施行。

title: 排污许可管理条例
summary: 为加强对排污许可管理、规范排污行为、控制污染物排放、改善生态环境而制定的行政法规，确立排污许可分类管理、申请与审批、排污管理、监督检查及按日计罚等严格法律责任。2020年通过、2021年3月1日施行，现行有效。
note: 2020年12月9日国务院第117次常务会议通过，2021年1月24日公布，2021年3月1日施行。
content_note: 内容校验不合格（title_mismatch:0.33），已标记重取

title: 地下水管理条例
summary: 为加强地下水管理、防治超采和污染、保障地下水质量和可持续利用而制定的首部地下水专门行政法规，规定调查与规划、节约与保护、超采治理、污染防治、监督管理及法律责任。2021年公布并施行，现行有效。
note: 2021年9月15日国务院第149次常务会议通过，2021年10月21日公布，2021年12月1日施行。

title: 太湖流域管理条例
summary: 我国首部流域综合性行政法规，为强化太湖流域水资源保护和水污染防治、保障防汛抗旱及用水安全而制定，规定饮用水安全、水资源保护、水污染防治、防汛抗旱与水域岸线保护、保障措施及法律责任。2011年公布并施行，现行有效。
note: 2011年8月24日国务院第169次常务会议通过，2011年9月7日公布，2011年11月1日施行。

title: 中华人民共和国河道管理条例
summary: 为加强河道管理、保障防洪安全、发挥江河湖泊综合效益而制定的行政法规，规定河道整治与建设、河道保护、清障、经费及罚则。1988年国务院令第3号发布，经2011、2017（两次）、2018年四次修订，现行有效。经核查，2023年国家层面未见修订。
note: 1988年6月10日国务院令第3号发布，根据2011年、2017年（两次）、2018年四次修订。用户提及的“2023年修订”经核查：国家层面2023年无修订，检索到的2023年地方发布系转载；个别省份（如山西省）2023年修订的是地方性《河道管理条例》，非国家级。据公开资料2026年1月或尚有修订，本次以官方公报可核范围（截至2018年四次修订）为准。
content_note: 内容校验不合格（title_mismatch:0.20），已标记重取

title: 取水许可和水资源费征收管理条例
summary: 为加强水资源管理和保护、促进节约与合理开发利用而制定的行政法规，规定取水许可分级审批、水资源费征收使用、监督管理及法律责任，是落实最严格水资源管理制度的重要法规。2006年公布施行，2017年修订，现行有效。
note: 2006年1月24日国务院第123次常务会议通过，2006年2月21日公布，2006年4月15日施行；2017年3月1日《国务院关于修改和废止部分行政法规的决定》修订。

title: 规划环境影响评价条例
summary: 为加强对规划的环境影响评价、从源头预防环境污染和生态破坏而制定的行政法规，规定综合性规划与专项规划环评、公众参与、审查、跟踪评价、区域限批及法律责任。2009年公布并施行，现行有效。
note: 2009年8月12日国务院第76次常务会议通过，2009年8月17日公布，2009年10月1日施行。

title: 防治船舶污染海洋环境管理条例
summary: 为防治船舶及其有关作业活动污染海洋环境而制定的行政法规，规定船舶污染物排放与接收、作业活动污染防治、污染事故应急与调查处理、损害赔偿及法律责任。2009年公布、2010年施行，历经2013至2018年六次修订，现行有效。
note: 2009年9月2日国务院第79次常务会议通过，2009年9月9日公布，2010年3月1日施行；经2013年（两次）、2014年、2016年、2017年、2018年共六次修订。

title: 供水条例
summary: 2026年新出台、取代1994年《城市供水条例》的行政法规，统筹城乡供水、强化从水源到水龙头全链条管理，规定供水水源保障、工程建设、经营服务、设施保护、应急管理与处置及法律责任。2026年2月公布、6月1日施行，现行有效。
note: 原清单称“城镇供水条例”。经核实，国家层面无独立“城镇供水条例”名称；2026年2月11日国务院总理李强签署第831号国务院令公布《供水条例》，自2026年6月1日施行，取代1994年《城市供水条例》。本条以《供水条例》对应原清单该项。

title: 南水北调工程供用水管理条例
summary: 为加强南水北调工程供用水管理、发挥工程经济、社会和生态效益而制定的行政法规，规定水量调度、水质保障、用水管理、工程设施管理与保护及法律责任，确立“先节水后调水、先治污后通水、先环保后用水”原则。2014年公布并施行，现行有效。
note: 2014年1月22日国务院第37次常务会议通过，2014年2月16日公布，自公布之日起施行。

title: 入河排污口监督管理办法
summary: 落实《入河排污口监督管理工作实施意见》，规范入河排污口设置审批、登记、监测、执法及整治，建立'受纳水体—排污口—排污通道—排污单位'全过程监管体系，是排污口监督管理的核心部门规章。

title: 饮用水水源保护区污染防治管理规定
source: 国家环境保护局（1989）；环境保护部（2010修正）
summary: 我国饮用水水源保护区制度的基础性规章，明确保护区划分、禁止行为、污染防治与监督管理要求，2010年由环境保护部令第16号修正，仍是水源地保护执法的重要依据。
note: 1989年发布，2010-12-22修正（环境保护部令第16号），现行有效未废止。；已抓取 PDF 原文：kb/pdf/2ac164a506ecea15.pdf

title: 突发环境事件应急管理办法
summary: 规范突发环境事件风险管控、应急准备、监测预警、应急处置与事后恢复，落实企业主体责任和属地政府责任，是水环境风险（含水源地突发污染）应急管理的核心规章。

title: 城镇污水排入排水管网许可管理办法
summary: 规范城镇污水排入排水管网许可的申请、审批与监督管理，明确雨污分流、预处理设施等要求，是城市生活污水源头管控与排水许可管理的部门规章，2022年修正后施行。

title: 建设项目环境影响评价分类管理名录（2021年版）
summary: 依法确定建设项目环评分类（报告书、报告表、登记表）管理依据，是水污染类建设项目环评审批的基础性规章，2021年版调整了部分涉水行业类别。

title: 排污许可管理办法
summary: 整合修订排污许可管理，落实排污单位'一证式'管理，明确申请、核发、执行报告、台账与证后监管，是与入河排污口监管衔接的水污染源管理的核心部门规章。

title: 企业环境信息依法披露管理办法
summary: 确立企业环境信息依法披露制度，规定重点排污单位等披露水污染物种类、浓度、总量及排放去向等义务，是水环境信息公开与信用监管的部门规章。

title: 关于水污染物排放标准执行问题的复函
source: 国家环境保护总局（办公厅）
summary: 就水污染物排放标准在环评、验收、排污许可中的执行口径作出解释，明确综合标准与行业标准的适用关系，是地方适用水污染物排放标准的重要参考文件。
note: 发文文号待核（国家环保总局办公厅复函，2001-06-29）；有效性待核。
content_note: 内容校验不合格（too_short:518），已标记重取

title: 重点排污单位名录管理规定（试行）
source: 环境保护部办公厅（现生态环境部办公厅）
summary: 按受污染要素将重点排污单位分为水、大气、土壤、声等五类名录，实行分类管理与年度动态筛选，是确定水环境重点排污单位并落实信息公开、自行监测要求的基础依据。
content_note: 内容校验不合格（title_mismatch:0.33），已标记重取

title: 环境监测数据弄虚作假行为判定及处理办法
summary: 明确篡改、伪造环境监测数据行为的情形认定与处理处罚规则，覆盖水质自动监测、手工监测等环节，是打击水环境数据造假、保障监测真准全的专门文件。

title: 水域纳污能力计算规程
source: 国家质量监督检验检疫总局、中国国家标准化管理委员会（水利部归口）
summary: 规定河流、湖泊、水库等水域纳污能力计算的技术要求与方法，为核定限制排污总量、入河排污口设置论证提供技术支撑，是水功能区水质管理的基础标准。
note: 全国标准信息公共服务平台（openstd.samr.gov.cn）可检索GB/T 25173-2010；具体页面链接待核。；原文链接待补（生态环境部官网）

title: 水功能区监督管理办法
summary: 规范水功能区划分、水质监测、限制排污总量意见、入河排污口监督及饮用水源区保护，是水利部门开展水域纳污能力核定与水质考核的专门办法。

title: 河湖生态流量管理办法（试行）
summary: 明确河湖生态流量（水位）确定、保障、监测与监管责任，将生态流量管控纳入流域治理与考核，对维持河湖基本生态功能、保障水生态安全具有重要意义。

title: 城镇污水处理提质增效三年行动方案（2019-2021年）
source: 住房和城乡建设部、生态环境部、国家发展改革委
summary: 部署加快补齐城镇污水收集处理短板，推进厂网河一体化、管网排查与提质增效，提升生活污水集中收集率与进水浓度，是城市黑臭水体治理的根源性举措。
note: 三年行动期（2019-2021）已结束，但文件作为政策依据仍具效力。

title: 城市黑臭水体治理攻坚战实施方案
source: 住房和城乡建设部、生态环境部
summary: 部署'十三五'城市黑臭水体治理攻坚战，提出控源截污、内源治理、生态修复、活水保质技术路线，明确到2020年地级及以上城市建成区消除比例达90%以上。
note: 住建部官网原文链接待核（索引号000013338/2018-00365）；此为天津市生态环境局转载PDF。

title: 深入打好城市黑臭水体治理攻坚战实施方案
source: 住房和城乡建设部、生态环境部
summary: 在2018版基础上深化，将治理范围由地级城市拓展至县级城市，强调防止返黑返臭长效机制，到2025年地级城市建成区长治久清、县级城市基本消除黑臭水体。

title: “十四五”城市黑臭水体整治环境保护行动方案
source: 生态环境部办公厅、住房和城乡建设部办公厅
summary: 立足生态环境监督职责，明确'十四五'城市黑臭水体整治环境保护行动的任务与方式，聚焦污水垃圾收集处理效能，建立问题清单并跟踪督办，支撑攻坚战成效。
note: 文号环办水体〔2022〕8号，生态环境部官网专题页；文件原文直接链接待核。；已抓取 PDF 原文：kb/pdf/b5e5e2fb97937db5.pdf

title: 农业面源污染治理与监督指导实施方案（试行）
source: 生态环境部办公厅、农业农村部办公厅
summary: 明确农业面源污染分区分类治理与监督指导思路，聚焦化肥农药减量、秸秆农膜回收、种植水产养殖污染治理，构建'源头减量—过程拦截—末端治理'体系。

title: 关于进一步明确畜禽粪污还田利用要求强化养殖污染监管的通知
source: 农业农村部办公厅、生态环境部办公厅
summary: 落实畜禽粪污资源化利用要求，明确还田利用标准（GB/T 36195、GB/T 25246等）、环评变更路径与台账管理，强化养殖污染事中事后监管，防范还田环境风险。
note: 贯彻落实《关于促进畜禽粪污还田利用依法加强养殖污染治理的指导意见》（农办牧〔2019〕84号）。

title: 关于进一步推进农村生活污水治理的指导意见
source: 生态环境部办公厅、农业农村部办公厅
summary: 以污水减量化、分类就地处理、循环利用为导向，健全县域治理机制，明确'三基本'成效评判标准，因地制宜选择资源化利用、纳管、集中处理模式，强化设施运维。

title: 地下水污染防治实施方案
source: 生态环境部、自然资源部、住房城乡建设部、水利部、农业农村部
summary: 提出'一保、二建、三协同、四落实'目标，部署地下水环境状况调查、保护区划分、加油站防渗改造、污染场地清单与修复试点，保障地下水型饮用水源安全。

title: 美丽河湖保护与建设行动方案（2025-2027年）
summary: 部署美丽河湖保护与建设，推动重要河湖生态保护修复、入河排污口整治、生态流量保障与幸福河湖建设，是新时代水生态环境治理的统领性行动方案。

title: 深入打好长江保护修复攻坚战行动方案
source: 生态环境部等十七部门
summary: 统筹推进长江水环境治理、水生态修复、水资源保障，强化总磷污染控制、入河排污口整治、岸线修复与磷矿尾矿治理，持续打好长江保护修复攻坚战。

title: 重点海域综合治理攻坚战行动方案
summary: 围绕渤海、长江口-杭州湾、珠江口等三大重点海域，部署陆海统筹的总氮削减、入海排污口整治、海水养殖与岸线治理，推动近岸海域水质改善。

title: 新污染物治理行动方案
summary: 系统部署新污染物调查监测、源头管控、过程减排与环境风险管控，涵盖全氟化合物等水体持久性污染物治理，对饮用水源与地表水新污染物防控具有指导意义。
note: 国务院办公厅文件，列入用户清单，作为水生态相关顶层治理方案纳入。

title: 全国集中式饮用水水源地环境保护专项行动方案
summary: 部署全国县级以上城市集中式饮用水水源地'划、立、治'专项行动，全面整治保护区内排污口、违法建设项目与网箱养殖，是水源地攻坚战的专项方案。
note: 以《关于印发〈全国集中式饮用水水源地环境保护专项行动方案〉的通知》印发，无单独发文字号。；已抓取 PDF 原文：kb/pdf/eeb9f6b6abe98ae1.pdf

title: 国务院办公厅关于加强入河入海排污口监督管理工作的实施意见
summary: 排污口排查整治的顶层文件，提出'查、测、溯、治'与分类整治，明确2023、2025年分阶段目标，构建'受纳水体—排污口—排污通道—排污单位'全过程监管。
note: 国务院办公厅文件，是入河入海排污口监督管理的统领性依据。

title: 入河（海）排污口三级排查技术指南等5项国家生态环境标准
summary: 发布排污口三级排查、无人机遥感航测与解译、命名编码及饮用水水源地风险源遥感调查5项标准，规范排污口排查整治技术方法，支撑专项行动落地。

title: 地表水环境质量标准
source: 国家环境保护总局/国家质量监督检验检疫总局

summary: 水生生物水质基准推导基本数据集系列标准之一，规范环节动物门（含寡毛类、蛭类）毒性数据要求，为水生态基准推导与底栖动物评价提供基础数据支撑。

title: 《水生生物水质基准推导基本数据集 第8部分：螠虫动物门》
summary: 水生生物水质基准推导基本数据集系列标准之一，规范螠虫动物门毒性数据要求，服务于水生生物水质基准推导工作。

title: 《水生生物水质基准推导基本数据集 第9部分：星虫动物门》
summary: 水生生物水质基准推导基本数据集系列标准之一，规范星虫动物门毒性数据要求，服务于水生生物水质基准推导工作。

title: 《水生生物水质基准推导基本数据集 第10部分：软体动物门》
summary: 水生生物水质基准推导基本数据集系列标准之一，规范软体动物门（螺、蚌等）毒性数据要求，为底栖动物及水生态评价提供基础数据。

title: 《水生生物水质基准推导基本数据集 第11部分：节肢动物门》
summary: 水生生物水质基准推导基本数据集系列标准之一，规范节肢动物门（含甲壳类、水生昆虫）毒性数据要求，为底栖动物评价与水生态监测提供支撑。

title: 《水生生物水质基准推导基本数据集 第12部分：棘皮动物门》
summary: 水生生物水质基准推导基本数据集系列标准之一，规范棘皮动物门毒性数据要求，服务于水生生物水质基准推导工作。

title: 《水生生物水质基准推导基本数据集 第13部分：脊索动物门》
summary: 水生生物水质基准推导基本数据集系列标准之一，规范脊索动物门（含鱼类）毒性数据要求，是水质基准推导中最常用的生物类群数据规范。

title: 《水生生物水质基准推导基本数据集 第14部分：浮游藻类》
summary: 水生生物水质基准推导基本数据集系列标准之一，规范浮游藻类毒性数据要求，与蓝藻水华预警和水体富营养化评价密切相关。

title: 《水生生物水质基准推导基本数据集 第15部分：大型藻类》
summary: 水生生物水质基准推导基本数据集系列标准之一，规范大型藻类毒性数据要求，服务于水生生物水质基准推导工作。

title: 《水生生物水质基准推导基本数据集 第16部分：水生维管束植物》
summary: 水生生物水质基准推导基本数据集系列标准之一，规范水生维管束植物毒性数据要求，支撑水生态修复与水生植被恢复评价。

title: 《水污染防治行动计划》（“水十条”）
summary: 以改善水环境质量为核心的十年期行动计划，提出到2020年七大重点流域水质优良比例达70%以上、地级及以上城市建成区黑臭水体控制在10%以内、集中式饮用水水源水质达Ⅲ类比例高于93%；部署全面控制污染物排放、节约保护水资源、严格环境执法监管等十大措施，是水生态环境治理的基础性文件。

title: 《重点流域水生态环境保护规划》
source: 生态环境部、国家发展改革委、财政部、水利部、国家林草局
summary: 经国务院同意，由生态环境部等5部门联合印发。按“河湖统领、三水统筹”思路构建水生态环境保护新格局，设水环境、水资源、水生态三大类11项指标（含3项约束性指标）；到2025年地表水Ⅰ—Ⅲ类比例达85%、劣Ⅴ类基本消除、县级城市建成区黑臭水体基本消除、354条（个）河湖达到生态流量要求。
note: 生态环境部发布稿；文号以五部门联合印发文件为准。

title: 统筹水资源、水环境、水生态治理 大力推进美丽河湖保护与建设（生态环境部部长署名文章）
summary: 生态环境部部长黄润秋署名文章，系统阐述《重点流域水生态环境保护规划》的战略意义、重点任务与主要举措，明确推动水生态环境保护由以污染防治为主向水资源、水环境、水生态等流域要素系统治理、统筹推进转变，是理解“三水统筹”与美丽河湖建设的重要权威解读。
note: 领导署名文章，属权威解读性文件，非规范性文件。

title: 生态环境部《重点流域水生态环境保护规划》政策解读系列
summary: 生态环境部对《重点流域水生态环境保护规划》的分主题解读，涵盖流域系统治理、河湖水生态保护修复、生态流量水量管理等内容，披露跨省重要江河生态流量保障目标批复、水量分配与河湖长制落实等进展，可用于起草、汇报时的口径参考。
note: 解读材料，非规范性文件。

title: 浙江省水污染防治条例
source: 浙江省人民代表大会常务委员会
summary: 2026年第四次修正，依据由《水污染防治法》等改为《生态环境法典》，是全省水污染防治主干法规。规定水环境质量目标考核、排污许可、流域协作、地下水与农业面源防治等。对杭州要求落实断面达标、入河排污口整治、总氮管控及数字治水。

title: 浙江省饮用水水源保护条例
source: 浙江省人民代表大会常务委员会
summary: 规范饮用水水源保护区划定、隔离防护、准保护区管控及污染整治。第三次修正后衔接《生态环境法典》。对杭州要求强化千岛湖、苕溪、钱塘江等饮用水源地保护，推进规范化建设与风险源排查。
note: 2026年第三次修正，具体公告链接待核

title: 浙江省河湖保护治理条例
source: 浙江省人民代表大会常务委员会
summary: 2025年12月通过、2026年3月1日施行，整合替代《浙江省河道管理条例》和《浙江省水域保护办法》，统辖河湖规划、保护、治理、利用，确立水域占补平衡与岸线管控。对杭州要求加强钱塘江、苕溪、运河等水域空间管控与幸福河湖建设。
note: zjrd.gov.cn 2025-12-24公布；公告第44号，2026-03-01施行，旧河道条例与水域保护办法同步废止

title: 浙江省水资源条例
source: 浙江省人民代表大会常务委员会
summary: 确立水资源刚性约束、用水总量与强度双控、节水优先及地下水管理。要求建立水资源承载能力监测预警。对杭州要求落实最严格水资源管理制度，保障城乡供水与生态流量。对杭州而言，应将该法规纳入依法治水管水框架，结合钱塘江、苕溪、千岛湖等本地水体特点，强化执法协同与考。
note: 2020-11-27通过，2021-01-01施行，具体链接待核；原文链接待补（人大法规公告栏目页）

title: 浙江省生态环境保护条例
source: 浙江省人民代表大会常务委员会
summary: 综合性生态保护主干法规，将'三线一单'分区管控、生态产品价值实现、生物多样性保护写入法治。对杭州要求落实分区管控、GEP核算与减污降碳协同。对杭州而言，应将该法规纳入依法治水管水框架，结合钱塘江、苕溪、千岛湖等本地水体特点，强化执法协同与考核问责。

title: 浙江省城镇污水集中处理管理办法
summary: 规范城镇污水集中处理设施的规划、建设、接纳与运行监管，明确排水许可与纳管要求。对杭州要求提升污水收集率、处理率与达标率，落实排水户许可与预处理。对杭州而言，应严格按规章落实许可、监管与处罚，并将要求嵌入市级实施办法与年度治水任务清单。

title: 浙江省跨行政区域河流交接断面水质监测和保护办法
summary: 建立上下游交接断面水质监测、考核与生态补偿机制，对超标断面追责并明确上游赔偿责任。对杭州要求落实与绍兴、金华、衢州等交界断面水质保障，支撑流域共治共保与横向补偿。
note: 省政府令第252号（2008-09-01施行），2021年第388号修正；zj.gov.cn公开文本

title: 浙江省建设项目环境保护管理办法
summary: 规定建设项目环评、'三同时'与竣工环保验收，将'三线一单'分区管控、生态红线与排污许可要求纳入。对杭州要求源头把好涉水项目准入，落实生态环境分区管控与总量控制。
note: 省政府令第288号公布，第321/364/388号修正；zj.gov.cn公开PDF

title: 浙江省环境污染监督管理办法
summary: 规范排污单位环境监管、在线监控与违法查处，配套水污染物达标管理。对杭州要求强化涉水企业执法与自动监测，支撑精准治污。对杭州而言，应严格按规章落实许可、监管与处罚，并将要求嵌入市级实施办法与年度治水任务清单。
note: 文号与日期待核（2015年修正）；原文链接待补（浙江省政府门户网）

title: 浙江省农村供水保障办法
summary: 替代原农村供水管理办法，确立城乡同质、县级统管原则，保障农村饮用水水质、水源保护与工程管护，并纳入绩效考核。对杭州要求提升农村供水水质，防范水源污染，衔接农村饮水安全。

title: 浙江省水生态环境保护“十四五”规划
source: 浙江省发展改革委、省生态环境厅等
summary: 明确十四五地表水优良率、断面达标、饮用水安全、水生态修复与总氮管控目标，部署入河排污口、黑臭水体与地下水任务。对杭州是编制市规划的顶层依据。对杭州而言，应衔接本规划目标，将任务分解落实到市治水规划与重点项目，强化断面达标与生态修复。
note: 浙发改规划〔2021〕210号，2021-05-31；zj.gov.cn与sthjt.zj.gov.cn均发布（含海洋规划同号文）

title: 浙江省海洋生态环境保护“十四五”规划
source: 浙江省发展改革委、省生态环境厅
summary: 部署近岸海域水质改善、入海河流总氮削减、美丽海湾建设与岸线整治。对杭州要求削减钱塘江口入海污染负荷，参与杭州湾协同治理。对杭州而言，应衔接本规划目标，将任务分解落实到市治水规划与重点项目，强化断面达标与生态修复。
note: 与省级水生态规划同号文（浙发改规划〔2021〕210号），2021-05-31，sthjt.zj.gov.cn发布

title: 浙江省八大水系和近岸海域生态修复与生物多样性保护行动方案（2021—2025年）
source: 浙江省人民政府办公厅
summary: 对钱塘江、苕溪、曹娥江等八大水系实施生态修复、岸线整治与生物多样性保护，建设美丽河湖与生态廊道，目标钱塘江干流Ⅱ类、千岛湖Ⅰ类。对杭州要求推进钱塘江—富春江—新安江生态修复。

title: 浙江省“三线一单”生态环境分区管控方案
source: 浙江省委、省政府（省生态环境厅印发）
summary: 全国首个经省委省政府审议发布的分区管控方案，划定2507个陆域、206个海洋管控单元，建立准入清单，创新工业项目分类表。对杭州要求落实水环境重点管控单元准入。对杭州而言，应制定配套细则与年度方案，把部署纳入治水考核、部门协同与数字闭环监管。

title: 浙江省生态环境分区管控管理实施细则
summary: 共八章29条，规范方案制定发布、5年定期调整与5年内动态更新、实施应用与数字化。对杭州要求依细则开展市级方案落地与跟踪评估。对杭州而言，应制定配套细则与年度方案，把部署纳入治水考核、部门协同与数字闭环监管。

title: 浙江省加强入河入海排污口监督管理工作方案
source: 浙江省人民政府办公厅
summary: 落实国家排污口整治，开展排查、溯源、分类整治与设置审批，依托'浙里碧水''浙里蓝海'建立'一张图'长效监管，2025年底完成全部整治。对杭州要求完成钱塘江、苕溪等入河排污口清零与规范化。

title: 浙江省美丽海湾保护与建设行动方案
summary: 部署34个美丽海湾'一湾一策'保护与建设，强化入海河流（钱塘江等7条）总氮总磷递进式削减与岸线整治，推进杭州湾等'三湾一港'综合治理。对杭州要求推进钱塘江口—杭州湾段美丽海湾协同建设。

title: 钱塘江流域水环境共治共保联盟盟约
source: 杭州、黄山、绍兴、金华、衢州五市政府
summary: 五市缔结治水盟约，组建协作小组，每年轮值并完成共治'十件事'（联合执法监测、河长巡河、白皮书等），跨市跨省协同。对杭州是流域共治核心机制。对杭州而言，应制定配套细则与年度方案，把部署纳入治水考核、部门协同与数字闭环监管。
note: 2023-11-14五市签署，含杭州、黄山、绍兴、金华、衢州

title: 城镇污水处理厂主要水污染物排放标准
source: 浙江省人民政府（省市场监管局发布）
summary: 全国领先提标：COD≤40、氨氮≤2(4)、总氮≤12(15)、总磷≤0.3 mg/L（括号内为每年11月1日至次年3月31日执行），其余执行GB18918一级A。对杭州要求污水厂清洁排放提标，支撑断面达标。
note: DB33/2169-2018强制性地标，2019-01-01实施；限值经多处环评文件核对；原文链接待补（地方标准备案信息平台）

title: 农村生活污水处理设施水污染物排放标准
source: 浙江省市场监督管理局
summary: 分一级/二级标准，基本控制项目pH、COD、氨氮、SS、总磷，选择控制总氮（封闭水体）、粪大肠菌群、动植物油；设计规模≥500m³/d执行GB18918。对杭州要求农村污水终端达标，防控面源入河。

title: 城镇“污水零直排区”建设技术规范
source: 浙江省市场监督管理局
summary: 全国首部'污水零直排区'建设省级地方标准，含总则、排查、设计与施工、评估验收、运行维护五部分，以'源—网—厂—口—河'为整体。对杭州要求依标创建，实现雨污全分流、污水全纳管。
note: DB33/T 2450-2022，2022-03-22实施，全国首部；省治水办制定，海外网报道

title: 美丽河湖建设规范
source: 浙江省市场监督管理局
summary: 由'河道建设规范'升级为'美丽河湖建设规范'，规定总体要求、安全工程、水环境治理、水生态保护修复、亲水便民与水文化等，新增数字化与湖泊分类。对杭州要求对标建设钱塘江、苕溪美丽河湖。
note: DB33/T 614-2023替代614-2016，2023-11-10实施；全国标准信息公共服务平台可查
content_note: 内容校验不合格（too_short:465），已标记重取

title: 海水养殖尾水排放标准
source: 浙江省人民政府（省市场监管局发布）
summary: 全国率先发布的海水养殖尾水强制性地标，对悬浮物、pH、COD、总氮、总磷设限值，新建即时、现有2025-10-15执行。对杭州湾养殖尾水管控具约束。对杭州而言，应依标开展建设、评估与运维，把标准要求纳入项目验收、长效管护与监测评价。

title: 《杭州市河湖保护治理条例》
source: 杭州市人民代表大会常务委员会
summary: 杭州河湖保护治理的最新地方性法规，整合《杭州市河道管理条例》《杭州市城市河道建设和管理条例》，明确河湖水域面积不减少、功能不减退的刚性要求，新增涵闸闸口停船、沿河设施悬挂晾晒等禁止行为，建立城市河道管理名录动态调整制度，并提出以视频监控、无人机、卫星遥感与数字孪生河湖提升智慧监管水平。施行后原两部河道法规同时废止。
note: 本条为全国人大系统媒体报道（人民网浙江频道），官方公布文本以杭州市人大常委会公告为准；已标注待核。

title: 《杭州市河道管理条例》
source: 杭州市人民代表大会常务委员会（浙江省人大常委会批准）
summary: 杭州河道管理的基础性地方性法规，规定河道（含江、河、湖泊漾荡、人工水道、行洪区、蓄洪区、滞洪区）整治、利用、保护及管理活动，明确市、区（县市）水行政主管部门为河道主管机关，实行统一管理与分级负责相结合。该条例在《杭州市河湖保护治理条例》施行后废止。
note: 中国法院网法规库全文；官方文本以杭州市人大常委会公布为准。

title: 《杭州市城市河道建设和管理条例》
source: 杭州市人民代表大会常务委员会（浙江省人大常委会批准）
summary: 规范市区城市河道及其附属设施（水域、河槽、堤防、护堤地、沿河绿地、配水泵站、船闸水闸及连通管涵等）的规划、建设、保护与管理，确立统一规划、综合保护、科学管理、生态优先、合理利用、共享开放原则，并明确城市河道具体名录由市建设、水行政、城市管理三部门协商提出、报市政府确定后公布。该条例在《杭州市河湖保护治理条例》施行后废止。
note: 杭州网转载全文（杭州市人大常委会公告第13号）。

title: 《杭州市生活饮用水源保护条例》
source: 杭州市人民代表大会常务委员会（浙江省人大常委会批准）
summary: 规定杭州市行政区域内生活饮用水源地保护工作，明确市、县（市）政府生态环境部门统一监督管理职责，划定一级、二级及准保护区并设立地理界标与警示标志，禁止在一级保护区内新建、改建、扩建与供水设施和保护水源无关的建设项目，禁止在二级保护区内新建排放污染物的建设项目及规模化畜禽养殖场、屠宰场。
note: 国家法律法规数据库（地方性法规库）PDF 全文，含2010年修改内容。
content_note: 内容校验不合格（not_chinese:0.00），已标记重取

title: 《杭州市湿地保护条例》
source: 杭州市人民代表大会常务委员会（浙江省人大常委会批准）
summary: 为对接《湿地保护法》而制定的市级配套法规，共5章33条。针对杭州重要湿地仅占湿地面积3.23%、96.77%为一般湿地的实际，将一般湿地细分为市级湿地、县级湿地和其他湿地并逐个确定管护责任单位，落实湿地面积总量管控制度与占补平衡要求，禁止占用市级、县级湿地（重大项目等除外）。

title: 《杭州市生态文明之都建设条例》
source: 杭州市人民代表大会常务委员会
summary: 全国首部聚焦“生态文明之都”建设的地方性法规，2025年10月1日起施行。将生态文明之都建设纳入法治轨道，与水环境保护、湿地保护、美丽河湖建设等形成制度合力，是杭州推进美丽中国先行区建设的标志性立法。
note: 据2025年度杭州市生态文明建设情况报告（2026-04-27）表述：该条例2025年10月1日施行，为全国首部。原文文本以杭州市人大常委会公布为准。

title: 《2025年杭州市国民经济和社会发展统计公报》（水环境部分）
source: 杭州市统计局、国家统计局杭州调查队
summary: 公报披露：市控以上断面水质Ⅲ类以上比例保持100%，杭州连续9年获得全省“五水共治”大禹鼎，森林覆盖率达65.74%；市区空气优良率85.8%，PM2.5平均浓度29.3微克/立方米。是领导参阅材料中可直接引用的年度权威口径。
note: 数据为年度初步数据；具体发布日期以政府网站页面为准（待核）。

title: 《杭州市地表水环境质量状况信息公开（2025年12月）》
summary: 全市地表水市控以上断面共95个，其中国控断面22个、省控以上断面39个；按 GB 3838-2002 表1项目评价（总氮、粪大肠菌群不参与评价），2025年1—12月国控、省控以上、市控以上Ⅰ—Ⅲ类断面比例均为100%。是断面达标考核与汇报中最直接的权威数据来源。
note: 月报信息公开页；发布日期以网站页面为准（待核）。

title: 《杭州市生态环境局高新区（滨江）分局2025年度工作总结及2026年工作计划》
source: 杭州市生态环境局高新区（滨江）分局
summary: 区级范例：2025年滨江区市控及以上断面年均水质优Ⅲ比例100%，考核交接断面、水功能区达标率及饮用水水源地水质达标率保持100%；开展重点河道问题排口溯源排查（完成率100%），推进黑臭水体整治环境保护行动并建立河湖水生态环境问题库，对钱塘江水源地（三江口）、白马湖备用水源地及滨江水厂开展水质与蓝藻监测，培育“美丽水细胞单元”试点。
note: 含“AI+环保”立体监测等做法，可作为区县案例参考。

title: 《杭州市湿地保护条例》实施情况（13.43万公顷湿地、保护率63.6%）
source: 杭州市林业水利局（新闻发布会）
summary: 杭州拥有近海与海岸湿地、河流、湖泊、沼泽及人工湿地5大类型，湿地面积13.43万公顷，湿地保护率63.6%；湿地面积、湿地保护率、湿地生态状况指数等保护成效指标已纳入高质量发展绩效评价体系，并出台湿地生态保护补偿实施办法、建立湿地保护专家委员会与志愿服务制度。
note: 新闻发布会报道，数据可作为参阅口径。

title: 《杭州市排水和再生水利用管理条例》
source: 杭州市人民代表大会常务委员会
summary: 杭州排水与再生水利用领域的地方性法规，涉及城镇排水许可、排水设施运行维护、再生水利用配置与管理等制度安排，与汛期排水管网溢流污染防控、再生水利用率提升等工作直接相关。原文链接与现行文号待补（见 note）。
note: 原文链接待补，此处为杭州人大网官方栏目页。

title: 《杭州市水生态环境保护“十四五”规划》
summary: 杭州市“十四五”时期水生态环境保护的目标、指标、重点任务与工程安排，落实国家《重点流域水生态环境保护规划》与浙江省水生态环境保护规划要求，涵盖断面达标、饮用水水源保护、入河排污口整治、水生态修复与美丽河湖建设等。需结合“十五五”流域水生态环境保护规划编制情况动态更新。
note: 原条目为占位链接，本次已降级为官方栏目页并标注待核；建议下一步补齐正式文号与原文直链。

title: 杭州市“五水共治”与河长制工作（含年度工作要点）
source: 杭州市治水办（市生态环境局、市林水局等）
summary: 杭州自2013年起实施治水“五水共治”（治污水、防洪水、排涝水、保供水、抓节水），连续9年获全省“五水共治”大禹鼎；配套河长制、湖长制实现河道分级分段全覆盖，并形成年度工作要点推进机制。是本平台跟踪杭州治水主线的核心抓手。
note: 原文链接待补，此处为杭州市政府门户网官方栏目页。

Received 6 September 2026│Accepted by M. Miliša: 14 September 2026│Published online 18 September 2026. 
 
 
Abstract 
Two new taxa of the water mite genus Hygrobates Koch, 1837 are described from Cyprus: H. dorflingeri n. sp. 
and H. ponticus cyprioticus n. ssp . Both belong to the H. calliger complex, whose members are common 
components of water mite assemblages in low-, middle-, and high-order streams. Phylogenetic analysis and ASAP 
species delimitation based on COI barcoding support their recognition as distinct lineages. Their morphological 
and genetic similarity to close relatives from mainland Anatolia suggests potential dispersal pathways for ancestral 
lineages during the colonization of Cyprus. 
 
Key words new species, DNA barcoding, taxonomy, Mediterranean. 
 
 
Introduction 
 
Hygrobates Koch, 1837 is the second most species- rich genus in the family Hygrobatidae . In the 
Western Palearctic, the genus is represented by two subgenera: the polyacetabulate Rivobates , 
characterized by a genital field with more than three, often numerous, pairs of acetabula, and the 
nominate subgenus, which is distributed across all continents except Antarctica (Smit 2020). 
Traditionally, in water mite literature, Hygrobates specimens with a coarse ly lineated soft 
integument have been assigned to H. calliger Piersig, 1896. This species was considered a common 
inhabitant of low -, middle-, and high- order streams with a Palearctic distribution (Matsumoto et al. 
2005; Gerecke et al. 2016). Pešić et al. (2022) first questioned the taxonomic status of H. calliger using 
an integrative approach based on standardized sequences of the cytochrome c oxidase subunit I (COI) 
gene. Their DNA barcoding study demonstrated that H. calliger represents a species complex consisting 
of several distinct, previously overlooked lineages. Some of these lineages (e.g., H. calliger Clades 1, 2,

and H. tyrrhenicus Pešić & Smit, 2022 from Corsica) appear to have a more restricted distribution. 
Tracking the spatial patterns of these lineages using Barcode Index Numbers (BINs), which act as 
reliable molecular surrogates for true species, provides valuable insight into their geographic distribution 
and the potential presence of cryptic or pseudocryptic diversity. 
In this study, we examined several samples belonging to the Hygrobates calliger complex 
collected in Cyprus. By combining morphological analysis with COI -based phylogenetic results, we 
describe and introduce herein one new species and one new subspecies. 
 
 
Material and Methods 
 
Water mites were collected during a field trip to Cyprus in May 2025. The specimens examined in this 
study were sampled from two sites within the Kouris River catchment on the southern slopes of the 
Troodos Massif. Detailed descriptions of these sampling localities are provided by Pešić et al. (2026c). 
Additional specimens were obtained by the third author during a macroinvertebrate sampling campaign 
aimed at assessing the ecological quality of Cypriot streams. 
Specimens were collected using hand nets and immediately preserved in 96% ethanol for 
molecular analysis. Following non-destructive DNA extraction, specimen vouchers were stored in 96% 
ethanol for morphological examination. Selected vouchers were subsequen tly dissected and slide -
mounted in Faure’s medium, while the remaining specimens were transferred to Koenike’s fluid for 
long-term storage. The holotypes and paratypes of the new species are deposited in the Naturalis 
Biodiversity Center, Leiden, The Netherlands (RMNH). 
Morphological nomenclature follows Gerecke et al . (2016). All measurements are given in 
micrometers (µm). Genital acetabula are measured on both sides and their values are given as a range. 
The following abbreviations are used: Ac = acetabula; BS = bootstrap support; Cx-I = first coxae; dL = 
dorsal length; H = height; I-L-1-6 = first-sixth segment of first leg; L = length; mL = = median length; 
n = number of specimens examined; P- 1 to P-5 = palp segment 1 -5; RMNH = Naturalis Biodiversity 
Center, Leiden; W = width. 
 
DNA barcode analyses 
Molecular analyses were conducted at the Canadian Centre for DNA Barcoding (CCDB; ccdb.ca) in 
Guelph, Canada. At this institution, the barcode region of the COI gene was sequenced using standard 
invertebrate DNA extraction, amplification, and sequencing protocols. In total, DNA was extracted from 
five specimens of the Hygrobates calliger complex (Table 1). Relevant voucher information and 
consensus sequences were deposited in the Barcode of Life Data Systems (BOLD) under the project 
DS-CYPHYD "DNA Barcodes of water mites of Cyprus" (dx.doi.org/10.5883/DS-CYPHYD).

In addition to the sequences obtained in this study, additional COI sequence data of Hygrobates 
calliger complex were obtained from Pešić et al. (2022, 2023, 2026a) and downloaded from the BOLD 
Systems public database. Sequence alignments were performed using MUSCLE (Edgar 2004). Intra - 
and interspecific genetic distances were calculated based on the Kimura 2 -parameter model (K2P; 
Kimura 1980) using MEGA 11 software (Tamura et al. 2021). The latter was also utilized to construct 
Maximum Likelihood (ML) trees. The best -fit substitution model (TN93+G+I) was selected using the 
Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) implemented in MEGA 11. Tree construction incorporated an 
initial Neighbour-Joining (NJ) tree and utilized the Subtree -Pruning-Regrafting - Extensive heuristic 
search algorithm (SPR level 5). Branch support was calculated using the nonparametric bootstrap 
method (Felsenstein 1985) with 500 replicates, with values shown adjacent to the branches. Codon 
positions included were 1st+2nd+3rd+Noncoding. 
Additionally, the sequence data were analyzed using the Assemble Species by Automatic 
Partitioning (ASAP), a method designed to species partitioning using a hierarchical clustering algorithm 
based on the pairwise distance distribution ( Puillandre et al. 2021). We used the online ASAP version 
(https://spartexplorer.mnhn.fr/) with default settings and K2P distance model. 
 
 
Results 
 
Species delimitation using DNA-barcodes 
The final alignment for species delimitation using COI sequence data included 57 sequences from the 
Hygrobates calliger complex, with H. fluviatilis (Ström, 1768) (NLACA1046-17) from the Netherlands 
used as the outgroup. This final alignment consisted of 1,221 nucleotide positions. The resulting ML 
tree is presented in Figure 1. 
The COI phylogenetic analysis revealed nine highly supported, species-level clades within the 
studied H. calliger complex dataset. Six of these corresponded to the six previously known clades of the 
H. calliger complex identified by Pešić et al. (2022): 
• H. calliger Clade 1 sensu Pešić et al . 2022 ( BOLD:AEF4261, BOLD:AET1162, 
BOLD:AEO0848, BOLD:AFE0075), distributed from Portugal to Greece and northwards to 
Norway; 
• H. calliger Clade 2 sensu Pešić et al. 2022 (BOLD:AEL5782), known from Germany and Russia 
southwards to Montenegro and Bulgaria; 
• H. calliger Clade 3 sensu Pešić et al . 2022 ( BOLD:AEK4718, BOLD:AEK4719, 
BOLD:AEK4720) from Calabria (Italy); 
• H. calliger Clade 5 sensu Pešić et al . 2022 ( BOLD:AEO5296), known from Germany and 
Russia southwards to Croatia; 
• Hygrobates tyrrhenicus Pešić & Smit, 2022 (BOLD:AEO1422) from Corsica (France); and 
• H. ponticus Pešić, Esen & Mumladze, 2022, known from Türkiye and Georgia. 
Within the H. ponticus lineage, three subclades can be separated. The first subclade includes 
three specimens from Cyprus representing a unique BIN ( BOLD:AHI8370), described herein as H. 
ponticus cyprioticus n. ssp. This subclade is recovered as sister to the lineage ( BOLD:AEO0649) that 
includes the nominotypical subspecies, H. p. ponticus , from eastern Türkiye and Georgia. The third 
subclade encompasses sequences of another subspecies, H. ponticus yildirimi Pešić, Zawal, Gülle, 
Cakmak & Saboori, 2023, which is known from two BINs: one from southwestern Türkiye 
(BOLD:AEY7516) and one from eastern Türkiye ( BOLD:AGO8960). The seventh lineage, which 
includes two specimens from Cyprus described here as H. dorflingeri n. sp., was revealed with a very 
strong support (BS = 99%) as the sister clade of H. turani Pešić, 2026 from eastern Türkiye. Finally, the 
ninth lineage encompasses sequences of H. anatolicus Esen & Pešić, 2013 from eastern Türkiye (Esen 
et al. 2013), represented by two BINs (BOLD:AEX2126 and BOLD:AEY8569). 
The average genetic distance between the clades recovered within the studied Hygrobates 
calliger complex dataset ranged from 12.28% (between H. dorflingeri n. sp. and H. turani) to 25.74% 
(between H. dorflingeri n. sp. and H. calliger Clade 1; Table 2). The average K2P distance between 
clades within Hygrobates ponticus varied from 8.64% (between H. p. cyprioticus n. ssp . and H. p. 
ponticus) to 10.25% (between H. p. cyprioticus n. ssp. and H. p. yildirimi ). The ASAP delimitation 
method identified molecular operational taxonomic units (MOTUs) that mostly matched the nine

DNA Barcode Analysis and Species Delimitation — The COI sequences form a unique cluster (BIN: 
BOLD:AHI8370), with the nearest neighboring BIN being that of H. ponticus ponticus 
(BOLD:AEO0649). The genetic distance between these two lineages was estimated at 8.64% K2P 
divergence, while the distance to the other subspecies, H. ponticus yildirimi, was estimated at 10.25% 
K2P (Table 2). 
 
Discussion — Molecular analysis revealed that the examined specimens from Cyprus represent a unique 
and well -supported COI clade. This clade appears to be genetically closer to the nominotypical 
subspecies from eastern Türkiye and Georgia than to H. ponticus yildirimi , which was originally 
described from southwestern Türkiye (Pešić et al . 2023). Given the allopatric distribution of the 
Cypriotic taxon relative to the two mainland subspecies, alongside its substantial genetic divergence (8.6 
to 10.3% K2P), we consider its status as a distinct subspecies justified. 
Morphologically, the new subspecies can be separated from both mainland subspecies. Females 
of the new subspecies exhibit a comparatively shorter gonopore, whereas it is distinctly longer and 
exceeds the length of the genital plate in the other two subspecies (see Pešić et al. 2022, fig. 10A; Pešić 
et al. 2023, fig. 1A). In males, the posterior margin of the genital plate has a small central protrusion 
within the indentation that extends beyond the posterior margin of the genital field, whereas it does not 
exceed the posterior margin in the other two subspecies (see Pešić et al. 2022, fig. 10C; Pešić et al. 2023, 
fig. 1B). Furthermore, according to its original description, Hygrobates ponticus yildirimi tends to have 
a longer ventrodistal projection on P -2 than the other two subspecies (L/W ratio: 1.2 vs. 1.0 in H. p. 
ponticus and H. p. cyprioticus n. ssp.). 
Distribution — Cyprus. 
 
 
Biogeographical Remarks 
 
Although the number of known water mite species from Cyprus is relatively limited (see Pešić et al. 
2026c for an overview), several significant characteristics of the water mite community and its faunal 
similarities with neighboring regions can be highlighted. The proximity of the island to mainland 
Anatolia appears to have facilitated colonization by species originating from the latter region.

12 
 
• Torrenticola baueri — Insular populations of this species belong to the same BIN that is widely 
distributed across mainland Anatolia and Iran (Pešić et al. 2025). Based on current knowledge, 
the Cypriotic populations represent the westernmost limit of the species' distribution. 
• Atractides nodipalpis complex — The A. nodipalpis-like populations from Cyprus belong to A. 
concavus Pešić & Smit, 2021, a species widely distributed across mainland Anatolia. This case 
represents a clear example of allopatric divergence at population level driven by geographic 
isolation. The Cyprus populations form a distinct Barcode Index Number (BIN: 
BOLD:AHI8403) with a 4.27% p-distance from the closest mainland BIN (BOLD:AEK3669), 
which includes individuals of A. concavus from southwestern Anatolia. While long-term insular 
isolation has resulted in a clear genetic break, evolutionary pressures likely have not yet caused 
these populations to diverge into a distinct species. 
• Hygrobates persicus — Recently, Pešić et al. (2026b) argued that colonization by H. persicus 
occurred significantly earlier than the final separation of Cyprus from the mainland (south-
central Anatolia), which took place during the Pleistocene –Holocene transition within the last 
2.6 million years (Yılmaz 2021). These authors suggested that the H. persicus populations on 
the island have likely not had sufficient evolutionary time to diverge into a distinct species. 
• Hygrobates calliger complex — High genetic distances indicate that both new taxa described 
in this study are the result of long-term genetic isolation. Both taxa have their closest congeneric 
relatives in mainland Türkiye (Anatolia), further supporting the hypothesis that ancestral 
lineages colonized the island well before its final separation from the mainland.

title: Environmental contamination and human health risk assessment of trace element exposure through diverse water sources
summary: Environmental contamination and human health risk assessment of trace element exposure through diverse water sources
content:
Environmental contamination and human 
health risk assessment of trace element 
exposure through diverse water sources
Saima Naz1*, Ahmad Manan Mustafa Chatha2, Qudrat Ullah3*, Muhammad Farooq4, Habiba Jamil5, 
HazratUllah Raheemi6 and Shakirullah Niazi7* 
Abstract 
Human activities such as industrial effluents, agricultural run-off, and other land-
based sources of pollution contaminate water with trace elements, posing threats 
to both the environment and human health. This study investigates concentrations 
of three trace elements, namely nickel (Ni), lead (Pb), and copper (Cu), in an assessment 
of health risks. The study comprised three different sources of water, namely surface 
water (SW), groundwater (GW), and industrial water (IW), sampled from six tehsils 
of District Bahawalpur, namely Bahawalpur, Bahawalpur Saddar, Hasilpur, Ahmedpur 
East, Yazman, and Khairpur Tamewali. A total of thirty water sampling sites, ten sites 
for each of the three types of water sources, were selected, and water samples 
were collected in the months of August, September, and October 2025. Results 
of the studied trace elements showed the highest concentrations in industrial water 
samples, followed by GW and SW samples (p < 0.001), with the highest concentration 
of Ni being 1.99 ± 0.20 mg/L, while that of Pb was 2.55 ± 0.11 mg/L and that of 
Cu was 3.24 ± 0.18 mg/L in IW samples. Significant differences were observed 
in the concentrations of the three studied trace elements in water samples as well 
as among the sampling sites of three types of water sources (p < 0.001). Estimated 
oral and dermal exposure (EEoral and EEderm) indicated low health exposure risks. 
However, THQoral values for Pb in GW and Ni, Pb and Cu in IW samples were found 
to exceed the acceptable threshold values. In addition to THQoral values, estimated 
cumulative non-carcinogenic health risks in the form of TTHQoral values for all three 
types of water sources under study were > 1 in all three water sources, suggesting 
potential risks. While, estimated carcinogenic health risks for the three types of water 
sources under study were found to be within the acceptable limits for all the studied 
health risks. This study provided a better understanding of various pollutants and their 
concentrations in water sources at the studied location.
Keywords: Water sources, Trace elements, Bioaccumulation, Pollution status, Health 
risk

1 Introduction
Water is an indispensable natural resource that sustains human health, ecosystem 
integrity, agricultural productivity, industrial development, and socioeconomic growth 
[11]. Although nearly 71% of the Earth’s surface is covered by water, freshwater accounts 
for less than 3% of the global water reserves, and only a small fraction is readily accessible 
for human consumption and domestic use [64]. Rapid population growth, urbanization, 
industrial expansion, agricultural intensification, and climate change have substantially 
increased the demand for freshwater resources while simultaneously accelerating their 
deterioration in quality [64]. Consequently, ensuring access to safe drinking water has 
become one of the foremost environmental and public health challenges worldwide 
and remains a central objective of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 6 
(SDG-6), which aims to ensure universal access to safe and clean water [28].
Among the numerous contaminants threatening freshwater resources, trace 
elements have received considerable scientific attention because of their persistence, 
non-biodegradability, environmental mobility, and potential to accumulate in aquatic 
ecosystems and living organisms. Unlike many organic pollutants that undergo 
degradation over time, trace elements remain in environmental compartments for 
prolonged periods and continuously cycle through water, sediments, soils, and biota. 
Their accumulation in drinking water has therefore become a major environmental 
concern owing to their adverse ecological impacts and their ability to cause long-term 
human exposure [3, 10], Vijay [63]. Increasing concentrations of trace elements in 
freshwater ecosystems have been associated with declining water quality, disruption of 
aquatic biodiversity, ecological imbalance, and growing risks to human health [41, 66].
Trace elements in aquatic environments are contributed by geogenic (natural) 
processes as well as by anthropogenic sources. Naturally, the metal-bearing rocks are 
weathered, minerals are dissolved, volcanic material is emitted, and soil is eroded to 
contribute to the surface water as well as to the groundwater. However, in recent decades, 
the anthropogenic sources have contributed to the majority of the contamination of the 
aquatic environments, i.e. industrial effluents, mining activities, municipal wastewater, 
agricultural runoff, fossil fuel combustion, metal processing industries, application of 
fertilizers and pesticides, landfill leachates, and rapid urbanization ecosystems [10, 52, 
62]. These contaminants, introduced into the environment through various sources, are 
transported to different aquatic environments through runoff, atmospheric deposition, 
infiltration and groundwater recharge, thereby degrading both surface and groundwaters 
[62]. The untreated industrial and municipal wastewaters are continuously being 
discharged into the environment, and in developing countries, the lack of wastewater 
treatment facilities adds to the contamination in aquatic environments [39].
The contamination of trace elements in water is creating serious health problems 
as these elements can easily enter the human body through water. Some of the health 
effects caused by chronic exposure to trace elements are neurological problems, kidney 
problems, cardiovascular diseases, liver damage, skeletal problems, reproductive 
problems, developmental abnormalities and various types of cancer [16, 17], Vijay [63]. 
Therefore, to ensure the health of the people and to provide safe drinking water, guideline 
values for trace elements in drinking water have been established by international 
organizations such as the World Health Organization (WHO) [43].
Page 3 of 23
Naz et al. Discover Environment (2026) 4:515 
 
Different trace elements have different biological functions and therefore they 
cannot be considered in a single group. While copper (Cu) is required for the human 
body in small quantities to carry out various physiological and biochemical activities 
like enzymatic activities, cellular respiration, antioxidant activities, formation of 
connective tissues, etc., high levels of this element can cause toxicity. It can cause 
disturbances in cellular activities, can cause increased oxidative stress, and can cause 
toxicity to the liver, kidneys, and gastrointestinal tract [19]. On the other hand, lead 
(Pb) is a non-essential element and has no known biological function in the human 
body. It is considered to be one of the most toxic elements found on the earth, and 
it causes cumulative toxicity to the human body. Even low levels of this element can 
cause toxicity to the human body after prolonged exposure. It can cause toxicity to 
the nervous system, blood, kidneys, heart, and reproductive organs [50]. While nickel 
(Ni) is naturally occurring and is widely used in various industrial applications, it 
is not required for the human body and can cause toxicity to the human body after 
prolonged exposure. It can cause various health problems like allergic skin reactions, 
respiratory problems, immunotoxicity, and carcinogenicity [16]. Therefore, it is very 
important to distinguish between essential and non-essential trace elements to find 
out their environmental behaviour, toxicological properties, and potential human 
health risks.
There is a constant struggle to provide safe drinking water in Pakistan as the country 
grapples to cope with the effects of rapid urbanization, industrial growth, lack of 
effective wastewater management, intensification of agricultural activities, and a surging 
population. Most of the country’s drinking water is sourced from groundwater, which is 
being continuously threatened and has thus become a matter of national public health 
concern, requiring adequate protection [46, 49]. Water from different sources, including 
surface water, groundwater, wastewater, and industrial effluent, is being contaminated 
with industrial waste, agricultural runoff containing a mix of agricultural chemicals, 
sewage from cities and mines, and geological processes of the natural environment [21, 
23]. Furthermore, the large volume of water being generated from seasonal flooding 
and uncontrolled urban growth is being freely discharged into all types of freshwater 
resources of the country and causing unprecedented water pollution, leading to 
widespread occurrence of water-borne diseases and serious chemical contamination 
[1]. National assessments conducted by the Pakistan Council of Research in Water 
Resources (PCRWR) have also demonstrated that a considerable proportion of drinking 
water sources fail to comply with recommended national and international water 
quality standards, highlighting the urgent need for continuous monitoring and effective 
management of drinking water resources [24].
Recent international studies have considerably advanced drinking water quality 
assessment by integrating trace element determination with pollution indices, 
multivariate statistical analyses, geospatial techniques, and quantitative human health 
risk assessment models. Such integrated approaches have enabled researchers to 
identify contamination sources, distinguish between geogenic and anthropogenic 
inputs, and evaluate both non-carcinogenic and carcinogenic risks associated with 
long-term exposure to contaminated drinking water. These comprehensive assessment 
frameworks provide a more robust understanding of the relationships between trace 
Page 4 of 23Naz et al. Discover Environment (2026) 4:515 
element contamination and public health and have become increasingly important for 
developing evidence-based environmental management strategies [42, 53].
In Pakistan, numerous investigations have assessed drinking water quality and the 
occurrence of trace elements in different provinces, including Punjab, Sindh, Khyber 
Pakhtunkhwa, and Balochistan. These studies have consistently demonstrated that 
industrial effluents, agricultural runoff, municipal wastewater, mining activities, and 
natural geological processes contribute substantially to trace element contamination 
in both groundwater and surface water [12]. Several investigations have further 
evaluated the potential human health risks associated with contaminated drinking water 
using hazard quotient (HQ), hazard index (HI), and carcinogenic risk (CR) models. 
While these studies have significantly improved the understanding of drinking water 
contamination in Pakistan, many have been limited to specific geographical regions, 
individual water sources, or selected contaminants [13]. Moreover, most investigations 
have primarily focused on reporting contaminant concentrations and basic health risk 
indices, whereas comprehensive comparisons among multiple water sources using 
integrated health risk assessment frameworks remain relatively limited [39].
Research worldwide is utilizing trace element determination, water pollution 
assessment indices, water quality statistics analysis, GIS spatial analysis, and human 
health risk assessment, etc., to evaluate drinking water source contamination, its 
causes, geogenic vs. anthropogenic, water quality health risks, etc. [42, 56, 58]. 
Comprehensive studies on drinking water source contamination assessment utilizing 
the above approaches have not only supported scientists and decision-makers in 
better understanding the relationship between water contamination by trace elements 
and water-borne health risks but also have enabled them in planning, designing, and 
implementing effective environment-friendly health management measures.
Nevertheless, contamination characteristics vary considerably among different 
geographical regions because of differences in geology, land use, industrial development, 
agricultural practices, and population density. Consequently, region-specific 
investigations remain essential for generating reliable baseline data and supporting local 
water quality management [7]. Despite these important advances, significant knowledge 
gaps remain regarding the distribution of trace elements and their associated human 
health risks in several rapidly developing regions of Pakistan. Southern Punjab, despite 
experiencing increasing urbanization, agricultural intensification, industrial growth, and 
expanding municipal activities, has received comparatively less attention than many 
other parts of the country. Bahawalpur District relies predominantly on groundwater 
for domestic consumption, while surface water and industrial water also contribute to 
meeting municipal, agricultural, and industrial demands. However, comprehensive 
information regarding trace element contamination across these different water 
sources and its potential implications for human health remains limited. To the best of 
our knowledge, no previous study has systematically compared groundwater, surface 
water, and industrial water within Bahawalpur District while simultaneously evaluating 
trace element contamination together with quantitative human health risk assessment 
using internationally accepted risk assessment models. This represents an important 
knowledge gap that must be addressed to support evidence-based environmental 
management and public health protection in the region.

Copper (Cu), lead (Pb) and nickel (Ni) are among the most common trace elements, 
which have been reported in various studies conducted on drinking water quality 
around the world. These trace elements occur in the environment due to geogenic as 
well as anthropogenic sources, such as industrial effluents, metal processing units, 
municipal wastewater, agricultural activities, corrosion of water distribution pipes, fossil 
fuel combustion and weathering of metal bearing rocks [37]. These elements can enter 
drinking water sources from these sources and can be used as indicators of water quality 
with reference to environmental hazards. Concentrations of these trace elements in 
drinking water are reported in the form of guidelines by national as well as international 
organizations. Other trace elements such as cadmium (Cd), arsenic (As) and mercury 
(Hg) are also considered as very toxic elements but have not been included in the present 
study, as Cu, Pb and Ni are very common, persistent in environment, having pronounced 
adverse health effects in human being and have been reported in vast number of studies 
all over the world. Moreover, these three elements are included in the drinking water 
quality guidelines all over the world and, therefore, inclusion of these three elements 
in the present study would provide a solid base to correlate concentrations of these 
elements with contamination as well as health risks to the consumers of water under 
study.
Unlike many previous investigations conducted in Pakistan that evaluated either 
groundwater or surface water independently or primarily reported contaminant 
concentrations, the present study adopts a comprehensive approach by simultaneously 
assessing trace element, copper (Cu), lead (Pb), and nickel (Ni) concentrations in 
groundwater, surface water, and industrial water collected from six tehsils of Bahawalpur 
District. Furthermore, quantitative human health risk assessment models were 
employed to evaluate the potential non-carcinogenic and carcinogenic risks associated 
with oral and dermal exposure to these trace elements through drinking water 
consumption. The findings provide a comprehensive baseline dataset for Bahawalpur 
District and contribute valuable scientific evidence for improving drinking water quality 
management, protecting public health, and supporting the sustainable management of 
freshwater resources in southern Punjab, Pakistan.
2 Materials and methods
2.1 Study area
This study investigated the concentrations of nickel (Ni), lead (Pb), and copper (Cu) in 
water samples collected from three major water sources, namely surface water (SW), 
groundwater (GW), and industrial water (IW), and evaluated the associated human 
health risks. Water samples were collected from representative groundwater, surface 
water, and industrial water sources located across six tehsils of District Bahawalpur, 
Punjab, Pakistan, namely Bahawalpur City, Bahawalpur Saddar, Ahmadpur East, 
Yazman, Hasilpur, and Khairpur Tamewali. The geographic coordinates of all 
sampling locations were recorded using a Global Positioning System (GPS) to 
facilitate site identification, spatial visualization, and future monitoring (Table  1). 
The corresponding tehsil for each sampling location was identified using reverse 
geocoding based on the recorded geographic coordinates. In total, the 30 sampling 
sites were distributed among Bahawalpur City (n = 6), Bahawalpur Saddar (n = 6), 
Page 6 of 23Naz et al. Discover Environment (2026) 4:515 
Ahmadpur East (n = 6), Yazman (n = 6), Hasilpur (n = 3), and Khairpur Tamewali 
(n = 3). The study area map (Fig.  1) was prepared using QGIS version 4.2.1 (Belém 
do Pará). Administrative boundary datasets at the provincial, district, and tehsil 
levels were obtained from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX) database (https:// 
data. humda ta. org/), while the hydrographic network (major rivers and canals) was 
incorporated using publicly available HDX waterway datasets. The georeferenced 
sampling locations were overlaid on the administrative boundary and hydrographic 
layers, and distinct symbols and colors were used to differentiate surface water, 
groundwater, and industrial water sampling sites. The final figure layout, including 
map composition, cartographic elements, annotations, and graphical refinements, 
was completed using Inkscape version 1.4.2 (f4327f4, 2025-05-13). Ten sampling sites 
were selected for each water source (SW, GW, and IW), and three replicate samples 
were collected from each site. Sampling was conducted between August and October 
2025.

2.2 Collection, transportation and storage of water samples
A representative sampling approach was adopted to collect water samples from 
three different water sources. Groundwater, surface water, and industrial water were 
selected as representative water sources because groundwater is extensively used 
for drinking purposes, surface water supports aquatic ecosystems and is widely 
used for domestic and livestock activities, while industrial effluents discharged into 
drainage channels ultimately enter freshwater systems and constitute a major source 
of trace element contamination. For each water source, ten sampling points were 
selected from different locations across the study area based on their accessibility 
and suitability for sample collection and transportation while ensuring representative 
coverage of the respective water source. Groundwater sampling points were selected 
from water pumps located within mosque premises because these water sources are 
routinely used by local communities for drinking and ablution purposes. Sampling 
points of surface water sources were selected from major canals in different 
geographical locations of the study area. Sampling points of industrial water sources 
were chosen from discharge points of active sugar mills, textile mills, flour mills, and 
oil mills. Industrial water samples were collected at the discharge outlets in the drain 
or the water body. This was done right after the water had been discharged into the 
drain or water body. The surface water and industrial water samples were collected 
at a depth of approximately 150 cm below water surface to minimize the influence of 
surface debris and floating contaminants.
The collected samples of water were stored in pre-cleaned high-density polyethylene 
(HDPE) bottles. Before the samples were collected, the HDPE bottles were cleaned 
with laboratory detergent and then rinsed with tap water, immersed in 5% (v/v) nitric 
acid solution for more than 24 h, and rinsed again several times with double-distilled 
deionized water. Each sample bottle was rinsed two to three times with water from the 
sampling site immediately prior to sampling in order to condition the bottle without 
diluting the sample because there might be some deionized water left in the bottle 
after cleaning. Field rinsing was done purely for conditioning purposes and not for the 
purpose of changing the concentration of trace elements. After collection of samples, 
bottles were closed, placed in a portable insulated ice box containing ice packs, and 
maintained at temperatures 6 ± 3 °C using ice packs during transportation. Samples 
were stored at appropriate conditions in the Zoology Laboratory, Government Sadiq 
College Women University, Bahawalpur for subsequent analysis.
2.3 Sample processing and digestion
A total of 90 water samples (30 samples from each water source) were collected from 
the selected sampling sites. These samples were analyzed for the concentration of Ni, 
Pb, and Cu to carry out human health risk assessment.
50 ml of each water sample was placed in a beaker and left to cool down. 1 ml of 
concentrated nitric acid (HNO₃; 69–72%) and 2.5 ml of concentrated hydrochloric 
acid (HCl; 30%) were added to the beaker, and the beaker was placed on a hot plate 
(Westpoint Double Hot Plate WF-262). The mixture was then heated to 90 °C and left 
to mix until the volume of the mixture had decreased to approximately 20 ml.
Page 9 of 23
Naz et al. Discover Environment (2026) 4:515 
 
After cooling, the solutions were filtered through Whatman No. 42 filter paper in 
a 100 mL volumetric flask. The solutions were then diluted to volume with deionized 
water. 2 mL of concentrated HNO₃ was added to the solutions to ensure complete 
acidification and to obtain clear solutions. The solutions were then diluted with 
3% (v/v) nitric acid according to the USEPA digestion protocol. After filtration and 
settling, the solutions were transferred into pre-cleaned sample containers which 
had been sterilized at 135°C. The samples were then sealed properly and stored until 
the start of the trace element analysis. For trace element analysis of digested samples 
Atomic Absorption Spectrophotometer (AAS), Analytik Jena NovAA 400P , at Central 
Laboratory, Muhammad Nawaz Sharif University of Agriculture, Multan, was used.
2.4 Determination of trace elements
Prior to analysis, the Atomic Absorption Spectrophotometer (AJ NovAA 400P , Analytik 
Jena, Germany) was optimized under the manufacturer’s recommended flame conditions 
for the determination of Ni, Pb, and Cu. Double-distilled and deionized water was used 
to prepare all working solutions and served as the reagent blank. Calibration standards 
of 0, 1, 2, 4, 6, and 8 mg L–1 were prepared from certified stock standard solutions. 
Calibration curves were generated by plotting absorbance against the corresponding 
standard concentrations and fitting the data using linear least-squares regression (y = a 
+ bx). Blank correction was applied prior to the quantification of sample concentrations. 
The concentrations of Ni, Pb, and Cu were determined according to the Standard 
Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater [4], Methods 3500-Ni B, 3500-Pb 
B, and 3500-Cu B). The trace element analyses were performed at an external analytical 
laboratory following the standard analytical protocol. Three independent water samples 
collected from each sampling location were analysed separately. One concentration value 
was obtained from each independently collected sample using AAS, and the results are 
presented as mean ± standard deviation (SD) of the three independent samples.

sites within the three water types was observed.
The range of concentrations for Ni, Pb, and Cu in surface water samples is shown

4 Discussion
In the present study, the concentration of Ni, Pb and Cu in surface water, groundwater 
and industrial water from six different locations in District Bahawalpur, Punjab, Pakistan 
was assessed, and their potential health risk to humans was determined. Our results 
showed a significant difference in the concentration of trace elements in various samples 
of water, and the highest concentration of trace elements was found in industrial water, 
followed by groundwater and surface water. Among the three trace elements, the highest 
concentration of Cu was found in industrial water and groundwater samples, followed 
by Pb in surface water samples. The highest concentration of Pb was found in surface 
water samples.
There is abundant evidence from Pakistan to support the fact that high concentrations 
of trace elements in groundwater and industrial water are because of high levels of 
industrial effluents, municipal wastewater, agricultural runoff, and natural geochemical 
processes [6, 32]. In developing countries like Pakistan, groundwater is the main source 
of drinking water for the majority of the population, whereas surface water is used for 
various purposes including domestic use, agriculture, and irrigation [38, 51]. Therefore,

degradation of these water sources is an issue of great environmental and health concern, 
as long-term exposure to high concentrations of trace elements could lead to health 
problems. Relatively low concentrations of trace elements in surface water may be due 
to dilution, high flow rates and dispersion of contaminants, whereas high concentrations 
in groundwater and industrial water may be due to accumulation of contaminants 
over long periods, limited natural dilution, and continued input of contaminants from 
anthropogenic activities [40].
The comparatively lower concentrations observed in surface water may be attributed 
to continuous water movement, dilution by rainfall and canal inflows, sedimentation 
processes, and shorter residence times, all of which reduce dissolved trace element 
concentrations. Nevertheless, surface water remains vulnerable to contamination 
through agricultural runoff, municipal wastewater discharge, atmospheric deposition, 
and urban stormwater, particularly during periods of intensive irrigation and seasonal 
rainfall [52]. These findings align with prior research that has reported similar results 
in various districts and regions across Pakistan. Numerous previous studies conducted 
within the country have also revealed the presence of high concentrations of dangerous 
metals in groundwater that is typically used for drinking [34, 36, 48].
Groundwater contamination is likely associated with the gradual migration of 
dissolved trace elements through soil profiles and aquifer materials. Leaching from 
contaminated surface environments, infiltration of agricultural runoff, seepage from 
industrial disposal sites, leakage from domestic wastewater systems, and weathering of 
local geological formations may collectively contribute to groundwater contamination. 
Because groundwater generally has a longer residence time than surface water, dissolved 
trace elements may accumulate over extended periods, resulting in comparatively 
higher concentrations. Furthermore, hydrogeological characteristics, including aquifer 
composition, soil permeability, groundwater flow dynamics, and recharge conditions, 
strongly influence the transport and persistence of trace elements within groundwater 
systems [62].
Agricultural activities also represent an important non-point source of trace element 
contamination within the study area. Long-term application of phosphate fertilizers, 
pesticides, livestock manure, and irrigation return flows may gradually enrich 
agricultural soils with trace elements that are subsequently transported into nearby 
surface waters through runoff or infiltrate groundwater through percolation. Therefore, 
the contamination observed in the present study is likely the combined result of 
industrial emissions, agricultural practices, domestic wastewater discharge, and natural 
geological processes rather than a single pollution source [10, 52, 55].
Environmental contamination by heavy metals is considered a major environmental 
problem, particularly in aquatic environments, due to their toxic nature. Moreover, 
the toxic effects of heavy metals increase with the presence of other heavy metals 
[33, 39]. In the present study, the atomic absorption spectrophotometric method was 
used to determine the concentration of heavy metals including Chromium (Cr), Iron 
(Fe), Nickel (Ni), Cadmium (Cd), Lead (Pb), Zinc (Zn), Cobalt (Co) and Manganese 
(Mn) in the water samples collected from the groundwater of industrial area of Kasur, 
Pakistan. The concentrations of these heavy metals were found to be higher than the 
water quality standards for these parameters as specified by World Health Organization

(WHO). The concentrations of heavy metals in the water samples of Kasur industrial 
area were found to be in the following order: Chromium (Cr) > Lead (Pb) > Iron (Fe) 
> Cadmium (Cd) > Nickel (Ni) > Cobalt (Co) > Manganese (Mn) > Zinc (Zn). Among 
these heavy metals, the concentration of Chromium (Cr) was found to be highest 
with an average value of 1.320 mg/L. The industrial area of Kasur is reported to be the 
major source of most of these toxic heavy metals [41]. In a study conducted in Sialkot, 
Pakistan, the concentrations of various heavy metals in the groundwater were found to 
be higher than the acceptable values specified by World Health Organization (WHO) 
for these parameters. These included concentrations of Nickel (Ni) at 0.10 mg/L, Copper 
(Cu) at 0.06 mg/L, Lead (Pb) at 0.49 mg/L, Manganese (Mn) at 0.03 mg/L, Iron (Fe) at 
0.30  mg/L, Chromium (Cr) at 0.03  mg/L and Zinc (Zn) at 0.16  mg/L. The area under 
study was divided into six regions. Based on the results, it was observed that the extent 
and causes of groundwater pollution were different in all the regions of the study area. 
In another study, the concentrations of lead in the untreated and treated surface water 
samples collected from 18 districts of Karachi were found to be within the permissible 
limits. The mean concentrations of lead in untreated and treated surface water samples 
were found to be higher in groundwater than in surface water (Haq et al. 2011).
This work found elevated levels of trace elements similar to a number of earlier 
surveys conducted in Pakistan. All of these studies reported widespread contamination 
of groundwater by human activities. Trace elements are among the more persistent 
environmental contaminants and can have toxicity for ecological organisms and human 
health. However, impact can vary greatly when more than one element is present at the 
same time [18, 39, 54]. Water from tubewells in Kasur industrial area contained levels 
of Cr, Fe, Ni, Cd, Pb, Zn, Co and Mn that were higher than the WHO recommended 
levels for drinking water by a factor of four to twenty-six. Industrial activities were 
the principal cause of these high levels [41]. Groundwater from Sialkot contained high 
levels of Ni, Cu, Pb, Mn, Fe, Cr and Zn that were above the WHO recommended levels 
for drinking water. The levels of these trace elements in groundwater from different 
parts of Sialkot were found to vary greatly (Ul Haq et  al. 2011). Seasonal variation in 
levels of trace elements in groundwater was reported in another study. In that work 
Pb, Zn and Cu were found to be the most persistent contaminating the groundwater 
during winter, while Ni and Cr were found to be the most persistent during summer; 
thus, hydrogeological factors as well as season could affect the distribution of these 
contaminants in groundwater [26]. Recently, it was reported that the levels of several 
trace elements in tube-well water from southern Punjab were at levels that could pose 
serious risks to human health [47]. A study that used water samples from rural tube-
wells in Tehsil Jhang found that 67% of the water samples from these locations contained 
levels of trace elements that exceeded the WHO recommended limits for these 
contaminants in drinking water [31, 33].
The significantly higher concentrations of Ni, Pb, and Cu observed in industrial 
water indicate that anthropogenic activities are the dominant contributors to trace 
element contamination in the study area. Bahawalpur has experienced increasing 
industrialization, including textile processing, metal fabrication, agro-based industries, 
fertilizer production, engineering workshops, and municipal wastewater discharge. 
Effluents generated from these activities may contain elevated concentrations of trace 
Page 18 of 23Naz et al. Discover Environment (2026) 4:515 
elements that are discharged directly or indirectly into nearby drains and water bodies. 
The elevated concentrations observed in industrial water therefore reflect continuous 
inputs from untreated or partially treated industrial effluents, whereas comparatively 
lower concentrations in surface and groundwater suggest dilution, natural attenuation, 
and geochemical filtration processes. Ni and Cu levels in the different water samples 
of the investigated area were found to be above the WHO recommended values for 
drinking water, for most of the samples (Fig. 2 and Table 2). These levels of contamination 
would mostly be due to increased industrial activities of industrialization, increased 
agricultural activities, the presence of untreated wastewater, and others that are known 
to cause the pollution of trace elements in Pakistan [2, 36, 57].
Jehan et al. [27] reported elevated levels of Pb and Cu in water samples from industrial 
estates of Pakistan. Concentrations of trace elements in industrial water are substantially 
higher than in surface water and groundwater. Industrial effluents are mostly untreated 
or are being treated inadequately, leading to the release of contaminated water into 
the environment. In aquatic systems, trace elements can accumulate in sediments and 
persist for long periods of time. These elements can be taken up by benthic organisms 
and get transferred to the upper food chain through aquatic food webs, posing ecological 
as well as human health risks [2, 22]. High levels of trace elements in sediments of Nullah 
Aik have been reported by Qadir et al. [45]. In the midstream section of the Nullah, the 
highest levels of trace elements were found in industrial effluents. In the present study, 
it was observed that industrial water contained higher levels of Ni, Pb, and Cu than 
groundwater and surface water, indicating that industrial activities are a major source of 
trace elements in the study area.
