regional and public monitoring networks. By engaging diverse stakeholders, it becomes 
possible to develop effective early warning systems and sustainable water management 
practices. This integrated approach not only enhances scientific understanding of water 
quality dynamics in monitored ecosystems but also equip local decision-makers with 
actionable insights to safeguard critical hydrosystems amid increasing environmental 
pressures.
5 Conclusion
Water quality is increasingly threatened by population growth, urbanisation, land-use 
change and climate-driven pressures. This review has synthesised the core literature on 
the evolution of water quality monitoring systems applied to aquatic ecosystems affected 
by turbidity and eutrophication, drawing primarily on peer-reviewed studies indexed in 
Web of Science. The analysed studies consistently highlight growing environmental and 
public-health risks associated with declining water quality.
In line with the hypotheses guiding this review, published monitoring practice in 
lakes and rivers remains dominated by grab sampling campaigns and satellite-based 
approaches, while continuous autonomous in-situ monitoring is comparatively less 
represented, except in rivers. At the same time, the literature reveals a persistent gap in 
accessible real-time information, particularly in regions with limited resources, where 
monitoring often depends on specialised technical capacity and uneven station cover -
age. Despite the increasing availability of affordable sensors capable of generating high-
frequency datasets, their systematic integration into coordinated monitoring networks 
remains limited. These insights suggest that the principal barrier to improving monitor -
ing is no longer technological availability but the institutional and operational integra -
tion of autonomous systems into structured observation frameworks. From a research 
perspective, the evidence supports deploying sensors both at basin scale and at strate -
gically selected locations within water bodies to capture spatial variability and identify 
pollution sources. Such configurations can strengthen model calibration, improve early-
warning capacity and enhance long-term environmental assessment.
To ensure future water security worldwide, two key public policy measures appear 
promising. On the one hand, the deployment of sensor networks in surface waters is 
crucial for preserving ecological processes while supporting socio-economic, produc -
tive, recreational and educational activities that depend on reliable water resources. On 
the other hand, the development of autonomous and participatory monitoring systems 
involving local communities could significantly improve real-time decision-making and 
promote more adaptive water governance.
In looking ahead, the decisive question will be whether systems can transform increas-
ingly available high-resolution data into effective environmental action alongside cur -
rent monitoring frameworks. Global challenges of water quality will thus require not 
only an effective data-to-decision chain, but also a broader transition from fragmented 
monitoring architectures towards more coordinated and responsive governance.

title: Review of: "Beyond Perplexity: The Quality–Memory Frontier of Native Mixed-Precision KV Caching in llama.cpp"
summary: Review of: "Beyond Perplexity: The Quality–Memory Frontier of Native Mixed-Precision KV Caching in llama.cpp"
content:
17 September 2026  ·  CC-BY 4.0
Peer Review
Review of: "Beyond Perplexity: The
Quality–Memory Frontier of Native
Mixed-Precision KV Caching in
llama.cpp"
Evgenii Arsentev1
1. Independent researcher
1. What the work claims
The paper adds native packed mixed-precision KV-cache types to a llama.cpp fork (Q3 in 32- and 64-
element blocks, and a 2-bit value format with a �xed four-level non-uniform codebook, NU-Q2), wires
them through CPU, cache-write and CUDA FlashAttention paths, and then asks what the quality–
memory trade-off looks like on Qwen3-4B-Instruct (Q4_K_M weights) on one 8 GB RTX 3070 Laptop GPU.
Two policies are proposed. The conservative one, Q4K-Q3V, stores 35,712 B/token, a 13.89% saving over
Q4K-Q4V (Table 2), and its paired differences on GSM8K, HumanEval and MBPP all have intervals
spanning zero (Table 5). The aggressive one, Q4K-MixV-21 (C2), stores 32,768 B/token, a 20.99% saving,
slightly lowers aggregate perplexity (Table 4, Wiki PPL 12.2435 vs 12.2919), but loses 2.81 points of strict
GSM8K accuracy with paired CI [−5.53, −0.08] and exact McNemar p = 0.047 (§5.2). A key-precision
ablation (Table 3) shows Q3-64 keys raise PPL by about 20% and Q2 keys collapse, while a 200-example
GSM8K pilot favours Q8 keys over Q4 keys by 13.0 points (77.5% vs 64.5%, p = 0.0007). The general thesis
is in the title and the last sentence of §10: perplexity-preserving KV compression is not necessarily
behaviour-preserving, so cache precision should be chosen on downstream and long-context evidence.
I want to credit several things up front, because they are uncommon. The byte accounting is exact: I
recomputed every row of Table 2 from §3.2 (L = 36, H_kv = 8, d = 128) and Table 1, and all six B/token
values and savings reconcile; for C2, keys 36 × 1,024 × 0.5625 = 20,736, values 4 × 1,024 × 0.5625 + 4 ×
1,024 × 0.40625 + 28 × 1,024 × 0.28125 = 2,304 + 1,664 + 8,064 = 12,032, total 32,768. The VRAM
measurements in §5.4 match the model too: 8,704 B/token × 32,768 tokens = 272.0 MiB, exactly the
Qeios
qeios.com doi.org/10.32388/XW3TTL 1
reported 32K gap, and 4,188 − 3,916 = 272. The downstream percentages are consistent with integer
counts (Table 4, GSM8K column: 65.43% = 863/1,319, 62.62% = 826/1,319, difference −37/1,319 = −2.81). And
Table 6, the failure ledger, is the most honest section I have read in a KV-quantization paper in some
time. A phantom uniform-Q2 control, "long-context" prompts that were only hundreds of tokens long, a
C2 map that silently ran as uniform Q4: these are exactly the bugs that quietly produce published results
elsewhere. Declining to copy numbers from other papers into a fake head-to-head (§2) is also the right
call.
2. Whether the conclusion holds on the data
The headline behavioural claim for C2 rests on one borderline test outside the declared con�rmatory
family. §4.4 declares the con�rmatory family as Q4K-Q3V on GSM8K, HumanEval, MBPP and 15 RULER
cells, with Holm correction, and says that "exploratory all-policy comparisons are not promoted to
con�rmatory claims." The C2 GSM8K result is not in that family. Yet §5.2 calls it "a borderline pre-
speci�ed result", and the abstract and §10 present it as the central demonstration. I could not �nd where
C2 versus Q4K-Q4V was pre-speci�ed. If C2 had its own family of the same 18 tests, the smallest Holm
threshold would be 0.05/18 = 0.0028; even restricted to the three downstream tasks it would be 0.05/3 =
0.0167. p = 0.047 clears neither. The paper half-concedes this ("would not survive an indiscriminate
correction"), but the abstract does not.
The thesis itself is not lost, in my reading. The stronger evidence for "similar likelihood, different
behaviour" is actually on the key axis: Table 3 gives Q8 and Q4 keys nearly identical PPL (Wiki 12.3683 vs
12.3227) with a 13.0-point GSM8K gap at p = 0.0007, and Table 4 shows the same direction at full size,
Q8K-Q8V 75.21 vs Q4K-Q4V 65.43 on GSM8K (992 vs 863 of 1,319, a 9.78-point difference) while Wiki PPL
differs by 12.2680 vs 12.2919. I would rebuild the argument around that contrast and report C2 as
supporting, exploratory evidence.
The frontier is conditional on Q4 keys, and the paper's own data say keys matter more than values.
Every proposed policy �xes keys at Q4 (§3.2). But the largest downstream effect in the paper is the Q8-vs-
Q4 key gap, roughly three to �ve times the C2 value loss (9.78 or 13.0 points against 2.81). Moving keys
from Q4 to Q8 costs 36 × 1,024 × (1.0625 − 0.5625) = 18,432 B/token by the paper's own accounting; C2
saves 8,704. A reader deciding where to spend memory needs Q8K-Q4V (59,904 B/token) and Q8K-Q3V
(54,144 B/token) evaluated on full GSM8K, HumanEval, and MBPP. Without them, calling Q4K-Q3V and C2
a "two-point deployment frontier" (abstract) overstates what was mapped: it is a frontier along the value
qeios.com doi.org/10.32388/XW3TTL 2
axis at a �xed, and apparently costly, key precision. There is also no FP16 cache reference anywhere.
Under Eq. 1 with 2 bytes per FP16 element, the default cache would be 36 × 8 × 128 × 4 = 147,456 B/token,
so Q4K-Q4V is already a 71.9% reduction whose quality cost is unmeasured.
"Statistically indistinguishable" is not the same as equivalent. Table 5 reports Q4K-Q3V minus Q4K-Q4V
intervals of [−1.06, 4.32] on GSM8K, [−4.88, 8.54] on HumanEval, and [−2.80, 4.40] on MBPP. The GSM8K
interval rules out a loss larger than about one point, which is good. HumanEval does not rule out a loss of
nearly �ve points, on 164 problems. §5.2 wording ("quality-preserving in the tested samples, not quality-
improving") is careful; the abstract's "statistically indistinguishable" and Table 7's "Reason/code
sensitive" recommendation lean further. A pre-stated non-inferiority margin, or simply putting the
lower bounds into the abstract, would �x this.
Aggregate PPL differences have no uncertainty attached. The abstract says C2 "slightly lowers held-out
perplexity." From Table 4, that is 12.2435/12.2919 − 1 = −0.39% (Wiki) and 18.3585/18.4667 − 1 = −0.59%
(OWT). §4.2 says a paired OpenWebText chunk analysis exists "only for its paired con�dence interval,"
but I could not �nd that interval reported. The same table has Q8K-Q8V with a worse OWT PPL than Q4K-
Q4V (18.5222 vs 18.4667), which suggests differences of this size sit inside run-to-run or chunk-level
noise. Without the interval, "slightly lowers" and "slightly improves" (§10) should become "does not
measurably change."
Three values look like possible copy or pipeline errors, and each touches a claim.
Table 4, HumanEval column: All-NU-Q2 V and Uniform-Q2 V both show 65.85 (108/164), while the
same two rows differ by 27.52 points on GSM8K (58.53 vs 31.01) and 17.20 on MBPP (48.00 vs 30.80).
Identical code scores for a collapsed and a non-collapsed cache are possible, but given that Table 6
records a "Uniform-Q2 phantom" where the control reused the non-uniform kernels, I would want the
per-problem outcomes and output �ngerprints for these two HumanEval runs speci�cally.
§6.4: on Qwen3-1.7B, "GSM8K falls from 65.43% to 62.02%." 65.43% is exactly the Qwen3-4B Q4K-Q4V
GSM8K score in Table 4. Two different models landing on the same 863/1,319 is not impossible. It is
unlikely enough that I suspect a transcription error.
Appendix B (Table 9), Q4K-Q4V variable tracking: 52 at 8K, 7 at 16K, 99 at 32K. A baseline that scores
7% at 16K and 99% at 32K on the same task points to something about the 16K generator or its
prompts rather than model capacity. The C2 "+60 points at 16K" in §5.3 is measured against this cell.
Q4K-Q3V (61, 14, 100) shows the same dip. Multi-key rising with context for the baseline (32.75, 35.25,
49.25) is odd too.
qeios.com doi.org/10.32388/XW3TTL 3
The paper's discussion of RULER (§5.3) already refuses to read the positive cells as "compression
increasing intelligence", which I appreciate. But "task- and context-dependent changes rather than
monotonic degradation" in the abstract is a claim about quantization, and it is hard to separate from an
artifact of the evaluation code until the 16K baseline dip is explained. There is also no high-precision
(Q8K-Q8V or FP16) RULER row to show what the model does at 16K with an uncompressed cache. The
"empirical self-resampling noise �oor" mentioned in §5.3 is never given as a number.
GSM8K scoring may con�ate formatting with reasoning. §4.3 uses "strict �rst-attempt exact match."
Quantization changes token trajectories (§5.3 says so), and a strict extractor penalises a correct answer
printed in a different format exactly as it penalises a wrong one. The paper interprets the C2 loss as
reduced "mathematical reasoning" (§1, contribution 3). Reporting a �exible-extraction score alongside,
or the share of failures that are unparseable, would show which of the two it is.
The layer-selection heuristic is never described. §3.2 gives the C2 map ({0, 7, 20, 23} at Q4, {9, 14, 16, 34}
at Q3-64) and §6.3 calls it "the heuristic", but I could not �nd what the heuristic is: a sensitivity score, a
PPL search, something else. §6.3 reports that C2 beats 30 of 32 random equal-memory maps on selection
PPL, and that Random-23 did better. Given that the paper's main message is that PPL does not predict
behaviour, selecting (or validating) a map on PPL deserves a sentence of re�ection. Random-23 appears in
RULER (Table 9) but its GSM8K score is not reported, which is the one number that would test whether
the choice of map matters for the mismatch.
The systems claims hold. Memory saving matches the analytic model to the MiB, and the 6.5% process-

title: Exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation and health-related quality of life in coronary artery disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis by exercise modality and disease status
summary: Exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation and health-related quality of life in coronary artery disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis by exercise modality and disease status
content:
【摘要】本库未获取到该文献全文，以下为出版方/索引库提供的官方摘要：

Exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation may improve health-related quality of life (HR-QoL) in patients with coronary artery disease (CAD), but whether responses differ by exercise modality and baseline disease status remains uncertain. We searched four English- and Chinese-language databases through September 2025 for randomized controlled trials comparing exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation with usual care or non-exercise controls in adults with CAD. Hedges’ g was pooled using a multivariate three-level random-effects model. Subgroup analyses examined exercise modality and baseline disease status, and certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. Fifteen reports comprising 16 trial comparisons ( N = 1,353) were included. Exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation was associated with improved HR-QoL (Hedges’ g = 0.89, 95% CI 0.46 to 1.33; p < 0.001). Larger point estimates were observed for combined aerobic and resistance training and for patients in the post-ACS stable phase. However, these subgroup comparisons were indirect, and the certainty of evidence was low to very low. Exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation may improve HR-QoL in patients with CAD, although the certainty of evidence remains limited. Findings regarding exercise modality and disease status should be considered hypothesis-generating rather than evidence of definitive subgroup superiority. title: Sleep quality is associated with gut microbiome signatures of hyperuricemia in Chinese elderly adults: a community-based case–control study
summary: Sleep quality is associated with gut microbiome signatures of hyperuricemia in Chinese elderly adults: a community-based case–control study
content:
【摘要】本库未获取到该文献全文，以下为出版方/索引库提供的官方摘要：

Hyperuricemia (HUA) has become a global health issue due to its rapidly increasing prevalence. Growing evidence from population and animal studies suggests that gut microbial dysbiosis and lifestyle changes are involved in serum uric acid metabolism. However, most existing studies are limited by small sample sizes or have yielded inconsistent findings. This study aimed to jointly investigate the associations of the gut microbiome, lifestyles, and dietary habits with HUA in Chinese elderly adults. A community-based case–control study was conducted across nine provincial-level regions in China, involving 617 participants. Data collection included lifestyle and dietary habit questionnaires, chronic disease history, serum uric acid (sUA) measurement, and 16S rRNA sequencing of fecal samples. Taxonomic composition and diversity analyses revealed significant difference between the HUA and controls in gut microbiota structure and diversity. Through differential abundance and co-occurrence network analyses, 42 microbial signatures associated with HUA or sUA were identified. Notably, the prevalence of g_Stenotrophomonas was positively associated with short sleep duration. A microbial risk score (MRS) model constructed using these signatures demonstrated an area under curve (AUC) of 0.761 in the discovery cohort and 0.675 in the validation cohort. Furthermore, a significant positive association was observed between sleep quality (sleep duration, number of awakenings, and short sleep duration) and the MRS model. These results add to the accumulating evidence implicating the role of gut microbiota and sleep in HUA, such as g_Stenotrophomonas , and inform the potential effect of the microbiome-based association between sleep duration and HUA. However, due to the cross-sectional design, we cannot infer causality from these associations, and the observed findings should be confirmed in prospective studies.

title: Integrated lignocellulolytic enzyme production and pretreatment of wheat straw by fungal consortium
summary: Integrated lignocellulolytic enzyme production and pretreatment of wheat straw by fungal consortium
content:
【摘要】本库未获取到该文献全文，以下为出版方/索引库提供的官方摘要：

In nature, fungi play a leading role in the biodegradation of organic waste by secreting a broad spectrum of lignocellulolytic enzymes (cellulases, hemicellulases, and ligninases). Inspired by this natural ecological synergy, in the present study, two promising fungal isolates, Trichoderma sp. isolate HR27 and Ganoderma sp. isolate HR31, were isolated and assessed for biocompatibility. Subsequently, their consortium was utilized for single-factorial optimization of various parameters (inoculum size, incubation time, lignocellulosic substrate, temperature, moisture content, pH, surfactant, nitrogen source, co-substrate, and inducer) under solid-state fermentation (SSF) using lignocellulosic waste for enhanced lignocellulolytic enzyme production. The results revealed that a significant increase in enzyme yield was achieved by utilizing wheat straw as the substrate, supplemented with 1.5 g/L Tween 80 and 0.5 mM CuSO4 in Asther’s medium with an initial pH of 3.5 at 30˚C. Compared to unoptimized media, optimized media resulted in 5.99, 5.18, 1.13, 2.57, 4.97, and 2.68-fold increases in endoglucanase, exoglucanase, β-glucosidase, mannanase, xylanase, and laccase production, respectively, on the fourth day of fermentation. Compositional analysis revealed that enhanced enzyme production under optimized conditions resulted in 31.7% delignification of wheat straw; however, only 22.9% was observed under unoptimized conditions, compared to that of the raw substrate. The removal of lignin resulted in higher exposure of cellulose (43.25%) and hemicellulose (24.85%) contents in wheat straw under optimized conditions. These findings highlight the potential of the fungal consortium as an effective candidate for lignocellulolytic enzyme cocktail production for various industrial applications using agricultural waste with concurrent valorization of agro-waste.

Czech Chem. Soc. Symp. Ser. 24, 325–344 (2026) Cena Karla Štulíka 2026 
340 
Janka Raganová, Agneša Szarka 
a Svetlana Hrouzková 
 
Ústav analytickej chémie, Fakulta chemickej 
a potravinárskej technológie, Slovenská technická 
univerzita v Bratislave, Radlinského 9, 812 37, Bratislava, 
Slovenská republika 
xraganova@stuba.sk, agnesa.szarka@stuba.sk 
 
Klíčová slova: bisfenol A, voda, endokrinne disrupčné 
chemikálie, LC­MS/MS 
 
● https://doi.org/10.54779/ccsss20260340 
 
 
Úvod 
 
Endokrinne disrupčné chemikálie (EDC) predstavujú 
skupinu látok, ktoré môžu narúšať hormonálnu reguláciu 
organizmov. Do vodného prostredia sa dostávajú rôznymi 
spôsobmi, napríklad pri nevhodnej likvidácii odpadov, 
zo splaškových vôd alebo sú priamo uvoľňované z poľno­
hospodárskych či priemyselných procesov 1. Jeden z vý­
znamných zástupcov tejto skupiny je bisfenol A (BPA), 
ktorý je jedným z najznámejších analógov bisfenolu, pou­
žíva sa vo veľkom rozsahu pri výrobe epoxidových živíc 
a polykarbonátových plastov. Fenolické zlúčeniny, vrátane 
BPA, sú produkované vo veľkých množstvách a dochádza 
k problému pri ich účinnom odstraňovaní pri úprave pitnej 
vody2. Čistenie odpadových vôd zohráva kľúčovú úlohu 
pri ochrane vodných ekosystémov a zdrojov pitnej vody. 
Bežne používané technologické procesy v čistiarňach od­
padových vôd, ako sú mechanické, biologické a chemické 
stupne čistenia, sú navrhnuté predovšetkým na odstraňova­
nie organického znečistenia, živín a suspendovaných lá­
tok3. Tieto konvenčné technológie však často vykazujú 
obmedzenú účinnosť pri eliminácii tzv. mikropolutantov, 
medzi ktoré patria aj EDC. V dôsledku toho sa látky ako 
BPA môžu len čiastočne odstrániť a následne sa dostávajú 
do povrchových vôd, kde predstavujú riziko pre vodné 
organizmy ako aj pre ľudské zdravie 3. Hodnotenie účin­
nosti čistiacich procesov a vývoj citlivých analytických 
metód sú preto nevyhnutné pre lepšie pochopenie správa­
nia sa týchto zlúčenín vo vodnom prostredí a pre optimali­
záciu technológií čistenia vôd. Konvenčné technológie 
čistenia vôd často nie sú dostatočne efektívne pri eliminá­
cii týchto mikropolutantov, čo vedie k ich perzistencii vo 
vodných ekosystémoch4. 
EDC môžu ohrozovať ľudí i voľne žijúce živočíchy 
rôznymi spôsobmi, pričom zasahujú do ich imunitného 
a endokrinné ho systému4. BPA je známy pre jeho toxiko­
logické riziko a má preukázateľné negatívne účinky aj pri 
nízkych koncentráciach5. Epidemiologické a experimentál­
ne štúdie poukazujú na súvislosť expozície BPA s výsky­
tom kardiovaskulárnych ochorení, poruchami plodnosti, 
narušením vývoja nervovej sústavy, ako aj s metabolický­
mi poruchami, ako sú obezita či diabetes mellitus 2. Okrem 
toho sa BPA spája aj s ochoreniami, ako je endometrióza 
či niektoré typy nádorových ochorení 6. Z toho dôvodu je 
nevyhnutné neustále vyvíjať analytické metódy určené na 
monitorovanie EDC v environmentálnych vzorkách. Na 
analýzu týchto zlúčenín sa využívajú rôzne chromatogra­
fické techniky, napríklad kvapalinová chromatografia spo­
jená s tandemovou hmotnostnou spektrometriou (LC -MS/
MS), HPLC vybavená spektrofotometrickým detekto­
rom v UV oblasti (HPLC -UV), alebo plynová chromato­
grafia s hmotnostnou spektrometriou (GC -MS). LC­MS/
MS je v súčasnosti považovaná za najvýkonnejšiu techni­
ku na analýzu BPA v environmentálnych matriciach7. 
Cieľom tejto práce bolo vyvinúť analytickú metódu 
na stanovenie BPA vo vodách pomocou techniky LC -MS/
MS a následne túto metódu aplikovať pri hodnotení účin­
nosti procesov odstraňovania BPA z vodného prostredia. 
 
 
Experimentálna časť 
 
Odstraňovanie bisfenolu A z vodných vzoriek bolo 
realizované pomocou UV žiarenia v laboratórnom fotoche­
mickom reaktore. Vzorky vody s definovanou počiatočnou 
koncentráciou BPA boli umiestnené do reakčných ná­
dob a vystavené pôsobeniu UV žiarenia. Ožarovanie pre­
biehalo za kontinuálneho miešania, aby sa zabezpečila 
homogénna expozícia celého objemu vzorky. V definova­
ných časových intervaloch boli odoberané alikvotné podie­
ly vzoriek, ktoré boli následne filtrované a analyzované 
pomocou LC­MS/MS metódy. Účinnosť UV čistenia bola 
hodnotená na základe poklesu koncentrácie BPA v závis­
losti od času expozície. 
Analýzy vzoriek vôd boli realizované pomocou kva­
palinového chromatografu Agilent 1260 Infinity II 
(Agilent Technologies, USA), ktorý bol spojený s hmot­
nostným tandemovým spektrometrom Agilent 6460 Triple 
Quad LC-MS/MS (Agilent Technologies, USA). Na sepa­
ráciu analytov sa použila kolóna ZORBAX RRHD Eclipse 
Plus C 18 (3,0 × 50 mm, 1,8 μm). Ionizácia analytov bola 
zabezpečená elektrosprejom v negatívnom ionizačnom 
režime a separácia iónov bola zabezpečená trojitým kvad­
rupólom ako analyzátorom pracujúcim v režime „multiple 
reaction monitoring“ (MRM). Chromatografická separácia 
bola uskutočnená za použitia gradientovej elúcie , pričom 
mobilnú fázu tvorili dve zložky: A – 0,05% kyselina mrav­
čia vo vode, B – acetonitril. 
ODSTRÁNENIE BISFENOLU A Z VÔD: LC-MS/MS STANOVENIE A HODNOTENIE 
ÚČINNOSTI ODSTRAŇOVANIA 
Czech Chem. Soc. Symp. Ser. 24, 325–344 (2026) Cena Karla Štulíka 2026 
341 
Výsledky a diskusia 
 
Pri vývoji LC -MS/MS (MRM) metódy na stanovenie 
BPA bol v prvom kroku zvolený vhodný prekurzorový 
ión. Ionizácia analytu bola testovaná v pozitívnom aj nega­
tívnom ionizačnom režime elektrosprejovej ionizácie (ESI), 
vyššia stabilita signálu a citlivosť boli dosiahnuté v negatív­
nom ionizačnom režime, ktorý bol následne zvolený pre 
ďalšie experimenty. V ďalšom kroku sa hodnotil vplyv 
napätia fragmentora na početnosť vybraného prekurzoro­
vého iónu. Vybrané napätie zabezpečovalo maximálnu 
odozvu signálu bez nežiaducich fragmentácií. Následne 
boli vybraté dva produktové ióny a kolízna energia pre oba 
produktové ióny. V tabuľke I sú zhrnuté testované a vybra­
né parametre LC-MS/MS MRM metódy. 
Vytvorila sa tak MRM metóda, ktorá bola následne 
použitá na analýzu kalibračných roztokov BPA priprave­
ných vo vode. Kalibračné roztoky boli analyzované v kon­
centračnom rozsahu od 0,05 po 10 ppm a každá koncentrá­
cia bola analyzovaná v troch opakovaniach. Závislosť 
koncentrácie BPA od odozvy detektora bola vyhodnotená 
pomocou kalibračnej krivky zostrojenej z priemerných 
hodnôt troch meraní. Linearita metódy bola vyjadrená 
prostredníctvom koeficientu determinácie, ktorého hodno­
ta dosiahla 0,9918, čo poukazuje na dobrú lineárnu závis­
losť v sledovanom koncentračnom rozsahu. 
Táto metóda bola následne použitá na analýzu vzoriek 
vôd s obsahom BPA, ktoré boli upravené pomocou UV 
žiarenia pri rôznych podmienkach. Porovnával sa obsah 
BPA vo vzorkách vôd pred aplikáciou UV žiarenia a po 
jeho aplikácii a vypočítal sa faktor účinnosti odstraňovania 
BPA (removal efficiency factor, REF). Analyzované boli 
dva typy vzoriek, ktoré sa líšili spôsobom úpravy použité­
ho katalyzátora. V jednom prípade bol katalyzátor sušený 
pri teplote 65 °C počas troch dní, zatiaľ čo v druhom prí­
pade bol katalyzátor spekaný pri teplote 550 °C počas 
12 hodín. Po ukončení čistiaceho procesu boli vzorky cen­
trifugované pri 6000 rpm počas 10 minút a následne prefil­
trované cez striekačkový filter s veľkosťou pórov 0,22 μm. 
UV žiarenie sa aplikovalo na degradáciu BPA pri rôznych 
časoch ožarovania, v prvom prípade (sušenie katalyzátora) 
v intervale od 30 do 120 min s inkrementom 30 min. V dru­
hom prípade (spekanie katalyzátora) v čase 10, 20, 30, 60, 
90, 120 min. Opakovateľnosť analýz bola vyjadrená po­
mocou relatívnej smerodajnej odchýlky a hodnoty sa po­
hybovali do 8 %. Účinnosť odstraňovania BPA bola vyjad­
rená pomocou REF, ktorý bol vypočítaný podľa rovnice 
(1). 
REFBPA = (1 – A/ARS) · 100 % (1) 
Výpočet REF je založený na porovnaní plochy chro­
matografického píku BPA vo vzorkách prečistenej vody 
(A) a plochy píku referenčného štandardu ( ARS), ktorým 
bola fortifikovaná vzorka vody s koncentráciou BPA 
10 ppm (ktorá sa následne čistila). Hodnota REF sa uvádza 
v percentách, pričom hodnoty nižšie ako 30 % indikujú 
nízku účinnosť odstraňovania BPA z vody a hodnoty vyš­
šie ako 70 % indikujú vysokú účinnosť odstraňovania. 
Na obr. 1 je znázornená závislosť hodnoty REF od 
doby pôsobenia UV žiarenia a spôsobu úpravy katalyzáto­
ra, uvedené hodnoty sú vypočítané z priemerných hodnôt 
troch meraní. Z výsledkov vyplýva, že pri použití sušené­
ho katalyzátora sa hodnoty REF pohybovali v rozmedzí 
20–28 %, čo indikuje nízku účinnosť degradácie BPA. 
Najvyššia hodnota REF (28 %) bola dosiahnutá po 30 min 
UV ožarovania, pričom s predlžujúcim sa časom expozície 
nedošlo k výraznému zlepšeniu účinnosti procesu. Nao­
pak, pri dlhších časoch ožarovania (60–120 min) bol za­
znamenaný mierny pokles účinnosti, čo môže súvisieť so 
zníženou fotokatalytickou aktivitou povrchu katalyzátora 
alebo s rekombináciou reaktívnych radikálov. 
Pri použití spekaného katalyzátora boli hodnoty REF 
vo všeobecnosti vyššie ako pri sušenom katalyzátore, čo 
poukazuje na významný vplyv tepelnej úpravy katalyzáto­

Výber parametrov LC-MS/MS MRM metódy

nia UV žiarenia a spôsobu úpravy katalyzátora 
Czech Chem. Soc. Symp. Ser. 24, 325–344 (2026) Cena Karla Štulíka 2026 
342 
ra na účinnosť fotodegradačného procesu. Hodnoty REF 
sa pohybovali v rozmedzí 18–42 % a najvyššia účinnosť 
bola dosiahnutá po 120 min UV ožarovania (REF = 42 %). 
Postupný nárast hodnoty REF so zvyšujúcim sa časom 
expozície naznačuje, že spekaný katalyzátor vykazuje 
stabilnejšiu fotokatalytickú aktivitu a lepšie podporuje 
tvorbu reaktívnych oxidačných medziproduktov zodpo­
vedných za degradáciu BPA. Nižšie hodnoty REF pri krát­
kych časoch ožarovania (10–30 min) naznačujú, že foto­
degradačný proces prebieha pomalšie a vyžaduje dlhší čas 
kontaktu UV žiarenia so vzorkou. Výsledky zároveň pou­
kazujú na skutočnosť, že samotné UV žiarenie v kombiná­
cii s použitým katalyzátorom nie je dostatočne účinné na 
úplnú degradáciu BPA pri zvolených experimentálnych 
podmienkach. 
 
 
Záver 
 
Predložená práca bola zameraná na vývoj LC-MS/MS 
metódy určenej na stanovenie BPA vo vodách. Vyvinutá 
metóda preukázala dostatočnú selektivitu a citlivosť a bola 
úspešne aplikovaná pri hodnotení účinnosti odstraňovania 
BPA z vodného prostredia. Zistilo sa, že UV žiarenie môže 
byť vhodným nástrojom na odstránenie BPA zo vzoriek 
vôd. Zároveň sa ukázalo, že pre komplexné posúdenie 
účinnosti čistiaceho procesu je nevyhnutné zamerať sa aj 
na zlepšenie ďalších podmienok prečistenia a na sledova­
nie vzniku a správania sa degradačných produktov BPA 
v prečistených vzorkách. Výsledky tejto práce poukazujú 
na význam kombinácie citlivých analytických metód a pokro­
čilých čistiacich technológií pri monitorovaní a odstraňo­
vaní endokrinne disrupčných chemikálií z vodného pro­
stredia. 
 
Táto práca bola podporená Agentúrou na podporu 
výskumu a vývoja na základe Zmluvy č. APVV -19-0149 
a SK-TW-24-0002. Práca bola tiež podporená Vedeckou 
grantovou agentúrou MŠVVaM SR a SAV na základe pro-
jektu VEGA 1/0378/26.

J. Raganová, A. Szarka, and S. Hrouzková 
(Institute of Analytical Chemistry, Faculty of Chemical 
and Food Technology, Slovak University of Technology in 
Bratislava, Bratislava, Slovakia): Removal of Bisphenol 
A from Water: Quantification by LC -MS/MS 
and Evaluation of Removal Efficiency 
 
This work focuses on the development of LC-MS/MS 
method for the determination of bisphenol A (BPA) 
in water samples. BPA is one of the endocrine disruptors 
with negative health effects and poses a significant risk 
to humans and ecosystem. An MRM method was 
developed and was applied to the analysis of water before 
and after UV treatment under various conditions. 
The efficiency was evaluated using the removal efficiency 
factor. The results showed that UV radiation in 
combination with catalyst can reduce content of BPA 
in water. 
 
Keywords: bisphenol A, water, endocrine disrupting 
chemicals, LC-MS/MS

title: Anomaly detection in smart agricultural control systems using semi-supervised bidirectional encoding
summary: Anomaly detection in smart agricultural control systems using semi-supervised bidirectional encoding
content:
【摘要】本库未获取到该文献全文，以下为出版方/索引库提供的官方摘要：

Anomaly detection is vital for maintaining the reliability of smart agricultural control systems, especially under conditions where sensor faults may disrupt automated irrigation and environmental monitoring. To address the limitations of traditional manual inspections and purely supervised methods, this study proposes DE-TabNet—a semi-supervised anomaly detection model based on bidirectional encoding. The model integrates temporal sequence learning via a BiGRU-VAE network and feature dependency extraction through a sparse autoencoder, forming an unsupervised feature fusion network. This representation is subsequently fine-tuned using a limited set of labelled data through a TabNet-based supervised module. Experimental evaluations on a real-world smart drip irrigation dataset demonstrated that DE-TabNet significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, including the DAGMM, iForest, VAE-LSTM, OCSVM, and Semi-TabNet methods. Specifically, DE-TabNet achieved up to 86.9% accuracy and an 80.8% F1 score, corresponding to improvements of 11.6% and 3.82%, respectively, over those of the baseline models. Additional validation on public datasets confirmed the model’s strong generalization ability, highlighting its practical value for robust anomaly detection in agricultural and other time series sensor systems.

summary: Superior reduction quality without improved outcomes: open versus closed reduction for displaced femoral neck fractures in adults under 60 years

Memorial Hospital, Taoyuan, Taiwan
Abstract
Introduction The optimal reduction strategy for displaced femoral neck fractures (DFNFs) in non-elderly adults remains 
controversial. Although open reduction may improve radiographic alignment, its impact on outcomes remains unclear. 
Materials and methods Adults aged < 60 years with DFNFs who were treated with internal fixation between 2017 and 2023 
were retrospectively reviewed. Patients were categorized into closed and open reduction groups. Reduction quality was 
assessed using the Garden alignment index and the Haidukewych reduction criteria. Multivariate analyses were performed 
for the overall cohort and patients with Pauwels type III fractures. Outcomes included non-union, osteonecrosis, femoral 
neck shortening, and major reoperations. 
Results In total, 98 patients were included, among whom 83 and 15 underwent closed and open reduction, respectively. 
Although open reduction achieved a higher rate of excellent reduction (53.3% vs. 16.9%, p = 0.012), it was not associated 
with lower rates of non-union or osteonecrosis. In the overall cohort, age was associated with non-union (odds ratio [OR], 
1.09; p = 0.024), whereas poorer reduction quality was associated with major reoperation (fair: OR 7.03, p = 0.012; poor: OR 
47.6, p = 0.007). In patients with Pauwels type III fractures, poorer reduction quality predicted conversion to arthroplasty 
(fair: OR 9.84, p = 0.014), and age was associated with non-union and osteonecrosis. Femoral neck shortening of > 10 mm 
at 3 months was associated with age and open reduction, whereas at 12 months, age and intraoperative blood loss remained 
significant predictors. 
Conclusions Open reduction achieved a higher rate of excellent reduction but did not reduce complication rates compared 
with closed reduction. Fracture severity, patient age, and reduction quality remained the principal determinants of outcome, 
supporting a fracture morphology-guided fixation strategy and realistic patient counseling.
Keywords Femoral neck fracture · Reduction quality · Reduction strategy · Femoral neck shortening · Fixation failure

Superior reduction quality without improved outcomes: open versus 
closed reduction for displaced femoral neck fractures in adults under 
60 years
Jia-En Chi1 · Chang-Heng Liu1 · Youh-Hua Lo1 · Chih-Yang Lai1 · I-Jung Chen1 · Yi-Hsun Yu1
Introduction
Displaced femoral neck fractures (DFNFs) in individu -
als younger than 60 years are uncommon, with an esti -
mated annual incidence of 4–72 per 100,000 people [ 1, 
2]. Although mortality is lower than that in older patients, 
these fractures typically result from higher-energy trauma 
and are often more severe [ 3, 4]. Moreover, disruption of 
the femoral head vascular supply is thought to contribute 
to an increased risk of non-union and osteonecrosis in this 
population [5]. Reported rates of treatment failure, includ -
ing fixation failure, non-union, symptomatic malunion, and 
osteonecrosis, vary substantially by fracture pattern, reduc-
tion quality, and fixation strategy, ranging from 5 to 90% 
1 3
 336 Page 2 of 10
Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery (2026) 146:336 
[6–9]. Approximately 15% of young adults with DFNFs 
eventually require conversion to total hip arthroplasty, usu-
ally within two years [9]. However, the age threshold defin-
ing “young” or “non-elderly” patients remains inconsistent 
across the literature. Although many studies have used 50 
years as the cutoff, contemporary treatment strategies fre -
quently extend head-preserving fixation to physiologically 
active patients approaching 60 years of age [10, 11].
Joint preservation is the goal of physiologically young 
patients; however, the optimal surgical approach remains 
debatable. Reduction quality is the most critical surgeon-
controlled determinant of outcomes and is strongly associ -
ated with uneventful union, whereas inadequate reduction 
increases the risk of treatment failure by more than five -
fold [6, 12, 13]. Although open reduction is often advocated 
to achieve anatomical reduction, pooled analyses have 
reported similar rates of acceptable reduction between open 
and closed techniques, with open reduction associated with 
higher rates of reoperation and complications [6, 12–17].
In contrast, closed reduction relies on fluoroscopic assess-
ment of alignment and displacement. Despite its presumed 
advantage in preserving femoral head vascularity, closed 
reduction has poor to moderate inter- and intra-observer 
reliability, limiting the reproducibility of reduction quality 
[18]. Postoperative femoral neck collapse, characterized by 
varus deformity or shortening, may result from inadequate 
reduction, unstable fracture patterns, injury mechanisms, or 
implant selection and is associated with poorer functional 
outcomes [19].
The purpose of this study was to compare the reduction 
quality and postoperative radiographic outcomes between 
closed and open reduction in adults younger than 60 years 
with DFNFs. The primary outcome was the reduction in 
quality, assessed using the established criteria. Secondary 
outcomes included radiographic stability, femoral neck col-
lapse and shortening, as well as fixation failure, including 
non-union, osteonecrosis, and major reoperations.
Methods and materials
Patient enrolment and data collection
Medical and radiographic records of patients younger 
than 60 years with DFNFs who underwent osteosynthesis 
between January 2017 and June 2023 were retrospectively 
reviewed using the Institutional Trauma Registry. Displace-
ment was defined as a Garden type III or IV fracture [ 20]. 
Patients with bilateral fractures, pathological fractures, or 
prior hip surgery were excluded.
Eligible patients were categorized into closed and open 
reduction groups based on the reduction technique applied. 
Demographic characteristics, injury-related variables, and 
operative details were systematically extracted from elec -
tronic medical records and operative reports. Attending 
orthopedic trauma surgeons or fellowship-trained surgeons 
performed all the surgeries. In cases where orthopedic 
residents participated as primary operators, the procedures 
were performed under the direct supervision of the attend -
ing orthopedic trauma surgeons. This study was approved 
by our Institutional Review Board (IRB No. 202600177B0).
Surgical strategy
Osteosynthesis was generally performed within 24 h of 
DFNF confirmation, unless contraindicated. The choice of 
closed or open reduction was determined by the treating 
surgeon’s clinical judgment based on fracture morphology, 
intraoperative reducibility, and overall patient condition.
For closed reduction, patients were positioned supine 
on a traction table, and reduction was achieved under flu -
oroscopic guidance (Ziehm Solo; Ziehm Imaging GmbH, 
Nuremberg, Germany), with provisional femoral head con -
trol using a percutaneously inserted Kirschner wire used 
as a joystick (Fig. 1). Reduction quality was assessed on 
anteroposterior and lateral femoral neck views, and defini -
tive fixation was performed after satisfactory alignment 
was confirmed. Fixation constructs included three or four 
percutaneous cannulated screws (CS, Syntec Technology 
Co., Hsinchu, Taiwan), a sliding hip screw (SHS) with an 
anti-rotation screw (Syntec Technology Co.), the Femoral 
Neck System (FNS, DePuy Synthes, Paoli, PA, USA), or the 
INTERTAN™ cephalomedullary nail (Smith & Nephew, 
London, UK).
For open reduction, the patients were positioned supine 
on a radiolucent table (Modular Table System, Mizuho OSI, 
Union City, CA, USA), and reduction was performed using 
the Smith–Petersen approach [ 21]. These procedures were 
primarily performed by senior orthopedic trauma surgeons 
with experience in femoral neck preservation surgery. After 
exposure of the anterior hip capsule, a Z-shaped capsulot -
omy was performed to directly visualize the fracture site 
and facilitate anatomical reduction. Care was taken to avoid 
excessive posterior-superior capsular stripping and to pre -
serve the retinacular soft tissues supplying the femoral head. 
Fracture fixation was then performed under combined direct 
visualization and fluoroscopic guidance. In most cases, an 
additional medial buttress plate (MBP) using a one-third 
semitubular plate (Syntec Technology Co.) was added to 
enhance stability (Fig. 2). Definitive fixation implants were 
otherwise identical to those used for closed reduction.

Postoperative image follow-up and rehabilitation 
protocol
Radiographic follow-up, including anteroposterior and 
lateral views of the hip, was routinely performed on 
postoperative day 1, as well as at 4 weeks, 3, 6, and 12 
months. Passive and active range-of-motion exercises of the 
affected hip were initiated immediately after surgery without 
restriction. Non-weight-bearing ambulation with crutches 
or a walker was prescribed for the first 4 weeks, followed by 
gradual progression to partial and then full weight-bearing

by 3 months, unless contraindicated. For patients unable to 
use crutches or a walker, such as those with concomitant 
upper-extremity injuries, ambulation was assisted using a 
wheelchair.
Applied classifications
Femoral neck fractures were classified using the Garden and 
Pauwels systems [20]. The Garden classification categorizes 
fractures into types I to IV based on fracture completeness 
and displacement [ 20]. Pauwels’ classification was deter -
mined according to the inclination of the fracture line rela -
tive to the horizontal plane: type I, < 30°; type II, 30°–50°; 
and type III, > 50° [20].
Reduction quality was assessed using two established 
indices. The Garden alignment index (GAI) was measured 
on postoperative anteroposterior and lateral radiographs to 
evaluate the alignment of femoral head trabeculae relative 
to the femoral shaft [ 22]. Based on the GAI, the reduction 
quality was categorized as anatomical, acceptable (155°–
180° in both views), borderline (< 155° or > 180° in either 
view), or unacceptable (< 150° or > 185° in the anteropos -
terior view).
Reduction quality was further evaluated using the Haid -
ukewych reduction criteria (HRC) [12]. The HRC provides 
a quantitative assessment of femoral neck fracture reduction 
based on the maximum residual displacement or angula -
tion measured on postoperative anteroposterior and lateral 
radiographs. Reduction was graded as excellent (< 2 mm 
displacement or < 5° angulation in any plane), good (2–5 
mm displacement or 5–10° angulation), fair (5–10 mm dis -
placement and/or 10–20° angulation), or poor (> 10 mm dis-
placement, > 20° angulation, or residual varus alignment).
Femoral neck shortening was assessed using radio -
graphic measurement methods described by Zlowodzki et 
al. and Polat et al. [ 19, 23]. Shortening was determined by 
comparing serial anteroposterior radiographs of the affected 
hip, and clinically relevant shortening was defined as a 
decrease of ≥ 10 mm. Posteromedial cortical comminu -
tion was defined as the absence of a continuous opposing 
posterior and medial femoral neck cortex on postoperative 
anteroposterior or lateral radiographs [16].
Interobserver reliability was assessed by two orthopedic 
trauma surgeons, with discrepancies resolved by a senior 
surgeon.
Definition of complications
Major complications included non-union, osteonecrosis, or 
major reoperations. Non-union was defined as the absence 
of radiographic healing at 6 months and/or loss of fixation 
integrity [ 24]. Osteonecrosis was diagnosed and staged 
according to the Association Research Circulation Osse -
ous classification [ 25], with stage III or higher considered 
a failure. Major reoperation included conversion to total 
hip arthroplasty or hemiarthroplasty, muscle pedicle bone 
grafting, or early fixation revision. Elective implant removal 
after fracture union was not considered a complication.
Statistical analysis
Data are presented as the mean ± standard deviation. All 
statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 
22 software (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY , USA). Continuous 
and categorical variables were compared using indepen -
dent t-tests and the chi-square test or Fisher’s exact test, 
respectively. Femoral neck shortening was measured using 
two-way ANOV A, and neck-shaft angle (NSA) was ana -
lyzed using the Mann–Whitney U test and Friedman test 
for inter- and intragroup comparisons at each time point. 
Intraobserver reliability was assessed using intraclass corre-
lation coefficients (ICC) (95% confidence interval [CI]) and 
Fleiss-Kappa (κ). Stepwise multivariate logistic regression 
was used to identify predictors of adverse outcomes. Statis-
tical significance was set at p < 0.05.
Results
Patient characteristics
During the study period, 98 patients met the inclusion criteria 
(closed, n = 83; open, n = 15) (Table 1). Patients in the open 
reduction group were younger (39.6 ± 12.2 vs. 46.3 ± 10.8 
years, p = 0.03). The open reduction group had a longer 
operative time (195.9 ± 47.0 vs. 130.2 ± 78.9 min, p = 0.002) 
and greater intraoperative blood loss (296.7 ± 262.2 vs. 
92.6 ± 199.4 mL, p = 0.001) than the closed reduction group. 
In the open reduction group, the primary fixation devices 
included cannulated screws in 12 patients, SHS in 1 patient, 
and FNS in 2 patients. Fourteen of the 15 patients addition-
ally received medial buttress plate augmentation, whereas 
1 patient underwent open reduction with cannulated screw 
fixation alone.
Complications and hip survival
During follow-up, osteonecrosis and non-union occurred in 
17 (17.3%) and 23 (23.5%) patients, respectively (Table 1). 
Non-union was more frequent in the open reduction group 
(46.7% vs. 19.3%, p = 0.04), whereas the incidence of osteo-
necrosis did not differ between the groups.
Overall, 30 patients (30.1%) underwent major reopera -
tion. Of these, 27 (27.6%) ultimately required conversion to

hip arthroplasty. The remaining 3 (2.5%) patients were suc-
cessfully treated with head-preserving salvage procedures. 
Major reoperation rates (46.7% vs. 27.7%; p = 0.22) and 
mean hip survival time did not differ significantly between 
the groups (p = 0.83). Two patients underwent early revision 
of internal fixation; salvage of fixation was achieved in one 
case, whereas the other later required arthroplasty because 
of non-union. Three patients underwent muscle pedicle 
bone grafting for non-union; successful salvage of fixation 
was achieved in one case, whereas the remaining two later 
required arthroplasty because of persistent non-union. One 
patient underwent core decompression with autologous 
bone grafting for early-stage osteonecrosis and was success-
fully salvaged.
Radiographic outcome
Postoperative radiographic outcomes are summarized in 
Table 2. Pauwels type III fractures were more prevalent in 
the open reduction group ( p < 0.001), whereas the preva -
lence of posteromedial cortical comminution was simi -
lar between the groups. Overall radiographic parameters, 
including postoperative displacement, neck–shaft angle, 
GAI, and femoral neck shortening, did not differ signifi -
cantly between the groups. Acceptable reduction according 
to GAI was achieved in 77.8%, and excellent-to-good reduc-
tion according to the HRC was achieved in 60%. Assess -
ment using the HRC demonstrated a higher proportion of 
excellent reductions in the open reduction group (53.3% vs. 
16.9%, p = 0.012).
Serial analysis of the NSA revealed progressive varus 
collapse in both groups. In the closed reduction group, 
the mean NSA decreased from 136.2° postoperatively to 
132.8° at 3 months and 131.7° at 12 months ( p < 0.001). In 
the open reduction group, the mean NSA decreased from 
136.1° to 127.4° and 129.0° at the corresponding time 
points (p = 0.001). Post hoc analyses showed that most varus 
changes occurred within the first 3 months, with no signifi -
cant progression thereafter.
Femoral neck shortening at 3 and 12 months was similar 
between the groups, with no significant differences observed

Multivariate analysis of complications in the overall 
cohort
Multivariate analysis of the overall cohort identified 
age as an independent predictor of non-union (odds ratio 
[OR] = 1.089, p = 0.024) (Table 3). Reduction quality 
assessed by the HRC and posterior cortical comminution 
were associated with conversion to arthroplasty, with fair 
and poor reductions conferring substantially higher odds 
than excellent reductions. Osteonecrosis was associated 
with patient sex (OR = 4.21, p = 0.043) but showed no sig -
nificant association with reduction-related variables.
Multivariate analysis in Pauwels type III fractures
Given the imbalance in fracture severity between the groups, 
additional multivariate analyses were performed in patients 
with Pauwels type III fractures (Table 4). Within this high-
risk subgroup, non-union was associated with older age, 
greater intraoperative blood loss, and poorer reduction, after 
adjustment for confounders. Osteonecrosis was associated 
with older age (OR = 0.935, p = 0.037). Reduction quality 
assessed by the HRC was associated with major reoperation 
(p = 0.032), with fair reduction conferring higher odds than 
excellent reduction (OR = 23.49, p = 0.005). Delayed sur -
gery showed a trend towards predicting major reoperation 
(p = 0.05). Femoral neck shortening > 10 mm at 3 months 
was associated with older age (OR = 1.132, p = 0.038) and 
open reduction (OR = 51.02, p = 0.01). At 12 months, older 
age and intraoperative blood loss remained significant 
predictors.

Discussion
Preservation of the native femoral head remains the pri -
mary goal in non-elderly patients with DFNFs because of 
the limited longevity and long-term consequences of hip 
arthroplasty in this population [ 26]. However, fixation fail-
ure remains common, with reported rates of non-union, 
osteonecrosis, conversion to arthroplasty, and reopera -
tion ranging from 9 to 30%, 14–18%, 14–24%, and 50%, 
respectively [ 9–11, 16, 27]. Although closed reduction is 
often preferred as the initial strategy because of its per -
ceived advantage of preserving femoral head vascularity, 
open reduction is sometimes required to achieve anatomical 
alignment in irreducible or highly unstable fractures. In our 
cohort, the overall outcomes, including non-union, osteo -
necrosis, reoperation, and conversion to arthroplasty, were 
comparable to those reported in contemporary series.
Achieving anatomical reduction in DFNFs remains 
technically demanding, regardless of whether closed or 
open techniques are used. Soft-tissue interposition, corti -
cal impaction, and unfavorable fracture morphology can 
prevent successful closed reduction, whereas three-dimen -
sional deformities, particularly residual varus or posterior 
tilt, are frequently underestimated on fluoroscopic assess -
ment [ 28, 29]. Previous studies have consistently demon -
strated that poor reduction quality is a strong predictor of 
fixation failure, with reported failure rates approaching 80% 
when acceptable alignment is not achieved [ 12]. In our 
cohort, fractures with relatively stable configurations were 
generally reduced and stabilized satisfactorily, whereas the 
most unstable patterns, predominantly Pauwels type III, 
were overrepresented among patients requiring open reduc-
tion. These vertically oriented fractures pose the greatest 
challenge to achieving and maintaining anatomic reduction 
and, therefore, warrant focused discussion of fixation strate-
gies in this high-risk subgroup.
Pauwels type III femoral neck fractures are character -
ized by high vertical shear forces and inherent instability. 
Accordingly, fixation constructs must provide robust resis -
tance to shear and rotation. Contemporary biomechanical 
and clinical evidence favors fixed-angle or angular-stable 
constructs, such as an SHS with anti-rotation screw (s) or 
the FNS, over multiple CSs in vertical fracture patterns 
[10, 30, 31]. An MBP has been proposed as an adjunct to 
enhance stability by neutralizing inferomedial sliding and 
converting shear forces into compression across the fracture 
plane, thereby improving the mechanical environment for 
union [32, 33].
In a large multicenter study of 565 young adults with 
DFNFs, Roser et al. reported higher failure rates with CSs 
(56%) than with fixed-angle constructs (36%). Among 
fixed-angle strategies, SHS combined with an anti-rotation 
screw and MBP demonstrated the lowest failure rate (11%), 
supporting the importance of implant selection and con -
struct stability in vertically unstable fractures [ 10]. In the 
present cohort, among the open reduction cases with MBP 
augmentation, cannulated screws were used more frequently 
than fixed-angle fixation, which may have contributed to 
the relatively high complication rate observed in the open 
reduction group. In selected cases, InterTAN was used as 
an angular-stable cephalocervical construct with integrated 
rotational control, and previous biomechanical studies have 
suggested its potential advantages in unstable Pauwels type 
III fracture models [34].
Importantly, the MBP was used as an adjunctive infero -
medial support rather than the primary load-bearing fixa -
tion construct. Overall construct stability still primarily 
depended on the lateral fixation device and fracture heal -
ing progression. In our failed cases, the predominant failure

pattern was early varus collapse associated with breakage 
of the medial plate, suggesting persistent mechanical load -
ing across the construct before fracture union. Therefore, 
although MBP augmentation may improve medial support, 
it may not fully compensate for insufficient lateral fixation 
stability in highly vertical and unstable fracture patterns. 
Given that the application of MBP generally requires open 
reduction, particularly in Pauwels type III fractures where 
indirect reduction is often insufficient, these unstable frac -
ture patterns remained prone to early femoral neck shorten-
ing and varus settling during the postoperative period.
In our cohort, the NSA decreased significantly from the 
immediate postoperative period to 3 months in both the 
closed and open reduction groups, with no further signifi -
cant progression. This temporal pattern aligns with prior 
reports showing that femoral neck collapse, manifesting as 
shortening and varus deformity, occurs predominantly in the 
early postoperative phase before plateauing [ 23, 35]. Chen 
et al. reported that most shortening occurs within the first 
1–3 months after fixation, whereas Polat et al. observed a 
median onset at 30 days, supporting the concept that clini -
cally relevant collapse represents an early mechanical phe -
nomenon rather than late loss of reduction [23, 35].
Therefore, the early decrease in the NSA observed in 
our study is more plausibly attributable to the mechanical 
settling of an intrinsically unstable intracapsular fracture 
under physiological load. Fracture characteristics such as 
high Pauwels angles, medial or posteromedial comminu -
tion, and residual varus alignment are well-established risk 
factors for early mechanical compromise and femoral neck 
shortening [ 13, 16, 23, 36, 37]. Accordingly, the greater 
early varus change observed in the open reduction group 
most likely reflects the preferential selection of more unsta-
ble fracture patterns rather than a detrimental effect of the 
open approach itself. Although concerns have been raised 
regarding greater soft-tissue disruption with open reduction, 
current evidence does not demonstrate a higher incidence 
of non-union or osteonecrosis attributable to open reduc -
tion and internal fixation [16, 38]. When performed through 
an anterior approach with a planned capsulotomy, such as 
the Smith–Petersen approach, preservation of the ascend -
ing cervical arterioles supplying the femoral head is achiev-
able, supporting the concept that osteonecrosis is primarily 
related to the initial fracture insult rather than to surgical 
exposure itself [39, 40]. Taken together, our findings suggest 
that the choice between closed and open reduction should be 
guided by fracture morphology and the ability to achieve 
stable anatomical reduction, rather than by the expectation 
of superior outcomes with either approach alone.
Despite efforts to minimize bias, this study had several 
limitations. First, the retrospective design carries the inher -
ent risks of selection and information bias, and the small 
single-center cohort may limit the generalizability of our 
findings. Furthermore, the reviewers were not fully blinded 
to the surgical approach because the implant configura -
tion was visible on the radiographs. Using 60 years as the 
upper age limit introduced greater heterogeneity in injury 
mechanisms and fracture characteristics, including a higher 
proportion of lower-energy injuries in older patients within 
the cohort. This may have influenced the treatment selec -
tion and complication profiles despite the subgroup analysis 
of Pauwels type III fractures. The modest sample size also 
limited the statistical power to identify independent risk fac-
tors after stratification by surgical approach. Because of the 
relatively small sample size and unequal group distribution, 
some analyses required non-parametric statistical methods, 
which may have reduced statistical sensitivity. In addi -
tion, the involvement of multiple orthopedic surgeons may 
have introduced variability related to differences in surgi -
cal technique and decision-making. The decision to perform 
open or closed reduction was not randomized. Therefore, 
selection bias is inherent. Although all procedures were 
performed or supervised by attending orthopedic trauma 
surgeons, surgeon-related variability in fixation technique 
and implant configuration could not be fully assessed in this 
retrospective study and may have influenced the postop -
erative outcomes. Radiographic assessment is the primary 
method for evaluating reduction quality and postoperative 
alignment; however, more precise modalities, such as com-
puted tomography, are not routinely available. Variations 
in patient positioning during radiographic acquisition may 
also have affected the angular measurements. Although a 
standardized postoperative weight-bearing rehabilitation 
protocol was recommended, actual compliance could not be 
objectively confirmed in every patient. Therefore, prema -
ture weight bearing may have contributed to early mechani-
cal failure in some cases. Future prospective multicenter 
studies with larger sample sizes and standardized imaging 
protocols, including advanced cross-sectional imaging, are 
warranted to better define the outcome determinants and 
validate our findings.
In conclusion in young patients with DFNFs, fracture 
morphology and patient age were more influential determi -
nants of outcomes than the choice between closed and open 
reduction. Open reduction achieved a higher proportion of 
excellent reductions but did not reduce complication rates 
compared with closed reduction, highlighting the impor -
tance of fracture morphology-guided fixation and realistic 
patient counseling.

title: Quality of life and university experiences of neurodivergent students in Brazilian higher education
summary: Quality of life and university experiences of neurodivergent students in Brazilian higher education
content:
【摘要】本库未获取到该文献全文，以下为出版方/索引库提供的官方摘要：

Neurodivergent students are increasingly represented in higher education, yet little is known about their quality of life and university experiences, particularly in middle-income countries. This study aimed to characterize the quality of life and academic experiences of neurodivergent university students in Brazil using a mixed-methods approach. This cross-sectional mixed-methods study included 80 neurodivergent university students enrolled in Brazilian higher education institutions. Participants completed the WHOQOL-BREF-ID, WHOQOL-DIS, and an open-ended questionnaire exploring university experiences. Quantitative data were analyzed using nonparametric statistics, and qualitative responses underwent reflexive thematic analysis. Students with co-occurring autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) reported significantly poorer psychological well-being than students with ASD alone, and lower social inclusion than students with ADHD alone. Higher socioeconomic status was associated with better environmental quality of life, social inclusion, and disability-related quality of life. Qualitative findings identified insufficient institutional support, academic demands, stigma, and barriers to social participation as major challenges, while also highlighting participants’ strengths and recommendations for more accessible and neurodiversity-affirming university environments. Neurodivergent university students experience persistent barriers that extend beyond academic accommodations to include social participation, institutional culture, and accessibility. The poorer outcomes observed among students with co-occurring ASD and ADHD, though preliminary, suggest that this subgroup may benefit from more individualized support. These findings support comprehensive, neurodiversity-affirming institutional strategies to promote inclusion and well-being in higher education.

title: Ecological Analysis and the Role of Forest Inventories
summary: Ecological Analysis and the Role of Forest Inventories
content:
【摘要】本库未获取到该文献全文，以下为出版方/索引库提供的官方摘要：

This contribution briefly reviews and discusses the evolution of forest inventories in Italy − a representative European country for biodiversity stock and landscape diversification. The role of forest monitoring in planning and sustainable management, especially in light of climate change, was specifically investigated. Given the increasing need to quantify the ecological value of landscapes and carbon stocks in agricultural and natural soils, the objectives, methodologies, and innovations of the main Italian forest inventories were described here and technical details discussed extensively. Starting from the first inventory (hereafter IFNI85) and moving to the second and the third survey (namely IFNC 2003 and INFC2015), the present work explores founding 74 criteria, sampling techniques, technologies used (e.g. GPS, dedicated software, geographic information systems), and the growing integration level of empirical data from remote sensing and ground surveys. The evolution and progressive alignment with international standards, in particular FAO statistics and CORINE Land Cover (CLC) mapping, emerged up to the present day, where forestry information is mainly disseminated via official platforms. The chapter finally highlights the growing importance of forest inventories for planning, ecosystem protection, and carbon assessment at both national and global levels.

title: Synthesis of Pd–ZnO-porous carbon photocatalyst and its application in rifampicin degradation for water remediation
summary: Synthesis of Pd–ZnO-porous carbon photocatalyst and its application in rifampicin degradation for water remediation
content:
【摘要】本库未获取到该文献全文，以下为出版方/索引库提供的官方摘要：

Nanocomposite photocatalysts have attracted considerable attention for the removal of pharmaceutical pollutants from aquatic environments. In this work, a palladium-decorated ZnO supported on porous carbon (Pd/ZnO/PC) nanocomposite was successfully synthesized and applied for the photocatalytic degradation of rifampicin (Rif) under UV irradiation. Porous carbon was prepared via phosphoric acid activation of potato starch, followed by ZnO deposition through a precipitation method and Pd nanoparticle incorporation. Structural and morphological characterizations (XRD, FTIR, SEM, and TEM) confirmed the successful formation of a well-dispersed Pd/ZnO/PC nanocomposite. Optical analysis revealed a band gap energy of 3.48 eV, indicating efficient UV-light activation. Photocatalytic experiments demonstrated a high Rif degradation efficiency of 98.80% after 180 min under a low-power 16 W UV lamp. To elucidate the adsorption and interaction mechanisms, molecular dynamics simulations were performed. The results revealed that porous carbon exhibits the strongest adsorption affinity toward Rif, while ZnO provides a stable adsorption platform dominated by electrostatic and van der Waals interactions. Radial distribution function and mean square displacement analyses further confirmed favorable adsorption configurations and enhanced molecular mobility with increasing temperature. The combined experimental and theoretical findings highlight the synergistic roles of porous carbon adsorption, ZnO photocatalysis, and Pd-mediated charge separation in the efficient removal of rifampicin from water.

title: Comparison of the psychometric properties of the Afaan Oromo versions of the EQ-5D-Y-3L and EQ-5D-Y-5L in Ethiopia
source: Health and Quality of Life Outcomes
summary: Comparison of the psychometric properties of the Afaan Oromo versions of the EQ-5D-Y-3L and EQ-5D-Y-5L in Ethiopia
content:
【摘要】本库未获取到该文献全文，以下为出版方/索引库提供的官方摘要：

The psychometric properties of the EQ-5D-Y-3L (Y-3L) and EQ-5D-Y-5L (Y-5L) have been compared across several countries; however, no evidence is available for the Afaan Oromo versions in Ethiopia. This study aimed to compare the psychometric properties of the Afaan Oromo versions of the Y-3L and Y-5L among Ethiopian children and adolescents with and without health conditions. The self-completed versions of the Y-3L and Y-5L were administered in a random order on two occasions (7 days apart) to assess test-retest reliability. Participants were children and adolescents aged 8–15 years with asthma, congestive heart failure, and acute lymphoblastic leukaemia, as well as school children and adolescents from the general population without known health conditions. Feasibility, ceiling effect, redistribution, and informativity were assessed using missing values, proportions reporting no problems, inconsistency between paired responses, and Shannon indices, respectively. Test-retest reliability was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) and Cohen’s weighted kappa. Known-groups validity was evaluated using the Kruskal-Wallis test. A total of 473 participants completed both instruments. The proportion of missing values was low for both the Y-3 L (3.8%) and Y-5 L (4.2%). The ceiling effect was lower for Y-5 L (47.2%) compared to Y-3 L (53.6%). The proportion of inconsistent responses ranged from 4.4% for the ‘feeling worried, sad, or unhappy’ dimension to 7.0% for the ‘looking after myself’ and ‘having pain or discomfort’. The Y-5 L demonstrated higher discriminatory power, indicated by a higher Shannon diversity index across all dimensions. Test-retest reliability was moderate for the Y-3 L (ICC = 0.70) and good for the Y-5 L (ICC = 0.80) based on level sum scores. The EQ VAS also showed good reliability (ICC = 0.85). Known-group validity was supported, as both versions distinguished school children from those with chronic health conditions and between different clinical severities. The Y-3 L and Y-5 L demonstrated comparable feasibility and confirmed known-group validity among children and adolescents in Ethiopia. The Y-5 L showed slightly better measurement performance by reducing the ceiling effect, improving discriminatory power, and demonstrating higher test-retest reliability. Although both instruments are suitable for use in the Ethiopian pediatric population, these findings suggest that the Y-5 L may be preferable when assessing HRQoL due to its improved measurement performance.

title: Comparative analysis of flood Forecasting using numerical Weather predictions and AI-based precipitation forecasts in the Solo River
summary: Comparative analysis of flood Forecasting using numerical Weather predictions and AI-based precipitation forecasts in the Solo River
content:
【摘要】本库未获取到该文献全文，以下为出版方/索引库提供的官方摘要：

This study evaluates the performance of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) Integrated Forecasting System (IFS) and the Artificial Intelligence Forecasting System (AIFS) in flood forecasting. The primary objective is to compare the accuracy of precipitation forecast products in predicting flood magnitude and arrival time. Hydrological simulations are conducted using the Rainfall–Runoff–Inundation (RRI) model, with all model configurations held constant except for the rainfall input. The evaluation of rainfall forecasts indicates that, at the same temporal resolution, the AIFS generally exhibits lower root-mean-square error (RMSE) and mean error (ME) than the IFS, although both forecasts tend to underestimate rainfall. Forecasted discharge results indicate that for the initial 24-hour lead time, there is no significant difference in RMSE between the IFS and AIFS. As the forecast lead time increases, AIFS shows superior performance with a progressively larger difference in RMSE. The F1-score and Frequency Bias (FB) consistently indicate more favourable results for AIFS compared to NWP across all lead times. The F1-score for AIFS ranges from 0.216 to 0.717, while IFS ranges from 0.121 to 0.692. The confusion matrix shows that the AIFS detects peak flood events more effectively than the IFS, producing a higher number of true positives, though this improvement is accompanied by an increase in false positives during non-flood periods.

title: The Definition of Escalation, and Unplanned Deaths as a Quality Metric
source: The Journal of Advanced Home Medicine
summary: The Definition of Escalation, and Unplanned Deaths as a Quality Metric
content:
Letter to the Editor 
The Definition of Escalation, and Unplanned Deaths as a Quality 
Metric 
Shauna Tierney, MD, CCFP1a 
1 Hospital at Home, Island Health 
Keywords: escalation, death, quality, metric, audit, decompensation 
https://doi.org/10.64919/001c.165108 
The Journal of Advanced Home Medicine 
Vol. 1, Issue 2, 2026 
To the Editors, 
I express gratitude to Dr. Iftah Amith for his valuable 
Letter to the Editor,1 and to JAHM for the opportunity to 
respond. 
Dr. Amith highlights the discrepancy between the defin-
ition of escalation provided by Ko et al2 and by ourselves,3 
and I agree that there is need for a consensus definition. Dr. 
Amith’s Letter then moves past this issue to propose his es-
calation audit framework, but I would like to explore this 
discrepancy further. 
I agree with Ko et al that an escalation is an “unplanned 
transfer to the BAM hospital.” Ko et al further specify that 
an escalation must involve an overnight BAM admission, 
but this requirement is superfluous. 
Escalations are of interest for many reasons: they put 
patients at risk of harm, they consume an inordinate 
amount of resources, and they can cause a type of moral 
injury to HaH staff. But it’s not all bad: escalations prove 
that HaH is fulfilling its mandate by caring for acutely ill 
patients, a percentage of whom will inevitably decompen-
sate. Whether an unplanned transfer to the BAM hospital 
involves an overnight stay does not change the fact that 
the transfer carries risk of harm to multiple parties while 
also demonstrating that HaH is in the business of providing 
acute care. 
Ko et al may have added the overnight admission re-
quirement to filter out returns to hospital to access BAM-
based resources only, without handing over responsibility 
for the patient’s care. To avoid this type of confusion, we 
include a transfer of care requirement in our definition of 
escalation, namely, An escalation is any unplanned transfer 
of care to the BAM hospital. 
The majority of Dr. Amith’s letter is devoted to his pro-
posed escalation audit framework, which appears to be an 
excellent tool for standardizing the analysis of escalations 
(and we appreciate that the framework includes non-
overnight BAM transfers). I would suggest that he remove 
the third domain (“Planned versus unplanned transfer”) be-
cause of the apparent consensus that escalations are, by de-
finition, unplanned. 
Lastly, I would ask the HaH Community to reflect upon 
where unplanned deaths belong in quality reviews. As 
stated in our original paper, we believe that escalations 
and unplanned deaths represent the same phenomenon, 
namely, a decompensation that HaH could not stabilize. 
Should HaH create a broader “decompensation” metric that 
includes both escalations and unplanned deaths? One with-
out the other can mask what is really going on, and both 
provide the same opportunity for quality improvement. 
CONFLICT OF INTERESTS 
None

title: Urban Expansion, Accessibility, and the Contribution of Spatial Analysis to Land-use Science
summary: Urban Expansion, Accessibility, and the Contribution of Spatial Analysis to Land-use Science
content:
【摘要】本库未获取到该文献全文，以下为出版方/索引库提供的官方摘要：

The present chapter investigates the relationship between urban expansion, accessibility, and land-use change, highlighting the contribution of spatial analysis to the study of forestation/deforestation dynamics associated with exurban development. The theoretical framework is delineated, referring to specific economic models and the forest transition theory, developing and discussing some criticisms to the Kuznets environmental curve in specific contexts. The methodology also proposes a practical exercise dealing with deforestation pattern in a metropolitan region, adopting a radial grid divided 30 into concentric bands and sectors to assess the variation in forest cover over a sufficiently long time period, namely from 1938 to 2006. The spatial analysis highlights the decisive impact of road axes and the lack of market instruments in preserving forest heritage. The results underscore the need for high-resolution spatial planning and public regulation interventions to promote the reversal of deforestation dynamics.

title: Preservice science teachers’ systems thinking skills, conceptual understanding, and system-level misconceptions: the water cycle system*
summary: Preservice science teachers’ systems thinking skills, conceptual understanding, and system-level misconceptions: the water cycle system*
content:
【摘要】本库未获取到该文献全文，以下为出版方/索引库提供的官方摘要：

This study explored the systems thinking skills (STS) and conceptual understanding of preservice science teachers (PSTs) related to the water cycle system. Research was designed as descriptive and correlational study with the use of two instruments -the Water Cycle Concept Map (WCCM) and the Water Cycle Diagnostic Test (WCDT). Data were collected from 254 PSTs from three universities. Concept map analysis revealed that most of the PSTs tended to rely on domino causality and encountered challenges in recognizing multiple causal patterns by using mutual and relational causalities. Cyclic causality was the second most commonly used pattern. WCDT scores showed that PSTs had both scientifically accepted conceptual understanding (seeing the oceans being the biggest moisture source, sun as the driving forces of the water cycle and human impact on the water cycle system) and system-level misconceptions (observed when they could not link physics, chemistry, biology and earth science knowledge correctly to explain the changes of water states in different processes (evaporation, condensation, cloud formation, and deposition). The relationships between STS and WCDT scores were found to be positive and of small to moderate strength, and pointed out that PSTs identified certain system relationships but their STS remained limited in terms of structural and procedural dimensions. This study suggested that teacher education programs should help PSTs to move beyond simply recognizing the components of the water cycle system and develop a deeper and more sophisticated understanding of the water cycle system.

Multiomics proﬁling identiﬁes molecular
